structured_description.about: Manager of the Operations Support Engineering (OSE) Electrical team at McGuire Nuclear Station, a two-unit PWR facility. Oversees a staff of degreed engineers and technical personnel providing electrical engineering support to station operations, reporting to the Engineering General Manager. Responsible for ensuring technical rigor, safety-first engineering practices, and staff development.
structured_description.responsibilities:
• Manage degreed engineers and technical personnel performing electrical engineering calculations, evaluations, system health monitoring, troubleshooting, and failure investigations
• Ensure technical conscience and engineering rigor commensurate with safety significance in all engineering products

• Determine maintenance strategies and work scope while supporting fleet and site reliability initiatives
• Ensure adherence to technical, administrative, and nuclear safety procedures and policies
• Assign capable personnel to OSE roles, provide training, and serve as rotational duty manager for Engineering
• Fulfill assigned Emergency Response Organization (ERO) role
• Observe staff performance, provide coaching, identify performance gaps, and develop closure solutions
• Identify opportunities for innovation and work elimination to improve departmental efficiency

• Work experience in electrical engineering, digital process systems, and/or cyber security
• Experience as a System Engineer

structured_description.about: Lead Duke Energy's Probabilistic Risk Assessment (PRA) Applications team to oversee risk-informed regulatory compliance, maintenance planning, and safety evaluations across nuclear sites. Direct PRA modeling strategy, NRC interface activities (SDP, LERs, LARs), and risk-informed Technical Specification evaluations. • Oversee Significance Determination Process (SDP) activities and serve as primary PRA interface with NRC Region II Senior Resident Inspectors
• Schedule bi-annual site leadership updates on PRA activities and maintain stakeholder communication across Operations, Regulatory Affairs, Engineering, and Training
• Manage budget, Notices of Enforcement Discretion (NOEDs), Licensee Event Reports (LERs), and License Amendment Requests (LARs) development and NRC transmittals
• Support Technical Specification 3.0.4.b risk evaluations and manage Phoenix Risk Monitor tool for work week scheduling and risk-informed decisions

• Lead team planning, resource allocation, and performance monitoring; identify process improvements and support external engagement with EPRI, PWROG, BWROG, NEI, and peer utilities
• Ensure technical reports, correspondence, and documentation meet company and NRC regulatory objectives per approved Safety Evaluations and NRC-approved methodologies
• Identify and support team training needs through seminars and work group-specific courses

• Bachelor of Science in Engineering from ABET-accredited program (or Master's degree in engineering)
• Minimum 7 years of engineering experience with at least 5 years directly in nuclear power industry
structured_description.desired:
• Minimum 3 years of PRA activities experience
• Knowledge of risk-informed applications: Risk-Informed ISI, Maintenance Rule, Mitigating Systems Performance Index (MSPI), NOEDs, SDPs, LERs, Component Risk Ranking, Time Critical/Time Sensitive Operator Actions, LAR development

structured_description.about: Travel-based Instrumentation & Electrical Technician supporting nuclear power plant operations across Duke Energy facilities in the Carolinas. You'll perform calibration, maintenance, and repair of electrical, electronic, pneumatic, and hydraulic instrumentation and control systems critical to reactor operations, with travel up to 100% of the time.
structured_description.responsibilities:
• Perform calibration, maintenance, and repair of electrical, electronic, pneumatic, and hydraulic instrumentation and control systems in a safe and reliable manner
• Execute assigned maintenance activities independently or within team settings; read and interpret I&C and electrical control drawings, work orders, and plans
• Communicate work progress and difficulties to co-workers and leadership; maintain housekeeping standards and ensure no reportable incidents in assigned areas
• Develop proficiency with calibration equipment, specialty tooling, and company software (Maximo, CAS, Tags Pro, eSOMs, Nantel)
• Understand and follow all applicable safety standards and use human performance tools; obtain and maintain unescorted nuclear access
• Assist in quality control and productivity management
structured_description.qualifications:
• High school diploma or equivalent
• One year of relevant work experience
• Successfully complete EEI's Power Plant Maintenance Selection System (MASS)
• Obtain and maintain nuclear facility access
• Obtain DOT medical card
• Ability to lift up to 50 lbs and work within 275 lb weight restriction
• Physical capability to stand, walk, stoop, climb ladders/stairs, work at heights, and work in confined spaces for extended periods
structured_description.desired:
• Experience with turbine/generator instrumentation
• One year closely related experience with electronic equipment
• Experience troubleshooting electrical and instrumentation equipment
• Experience reading electrical diagrams, schematics, and one-line drawings
• Experience utilizing electrical and instrumentation test equipment
• Experience with lockout/tagout procedures
• Current nuclear access
structured_description.location_details: Based at nuclear facilities in NC or SC; up to 100% travel required; must live within reasonable daily commute to assigned location; shift work, weekends, and overtime expected; exposure to extreme weather, high temperatures/pressures, rotating machinery, and confined spaces.

structured_description.about: Electrical/Instrumentation & Control (I&C) Engineer at Harris Nuclear Plant supporting maintenance engineering for a Westinghouse PWR (2948 MWth). This Engineer III or Senior Engineer role focuses on electrical system reliability, component maintenance planning, troubleshooting, and operability determinations with independent work capability and mentoring responsibilities.
structured_description.responsibilities:
• Provide engineering expertise in identification, analysis, and resolution of electrical system problems of increasing scope and complexity
• Support troubleshooting, evaluate equipment degradation, and coordinate component reliability improvements using Preventive Maintenance, Condition-Based Maintenance, and Predictive Maintenance techniques
• Serve as designated owner for assigned electrical systems and provide tactical day-to-day maintenance engineering support
• Plan, organize, estimate, schedule, and monitor work activities to accomplish business goals and manage decisions affecting operations
• Prepare thorough technical reports, correspondence, and documentation with analysis capability for complex problems
• Conduct engineering investigations with full technical responsibility for planning and coordinating problem resolution
• Provide equipment technical support for Operability Determinations and support review of Operations and Maintenance procedures
• Analyze and recommend enhancements to business processes; stay current with nuclear industry developments and technologies
• Coordinate work effectively across teams and demonstrate strong oral and written communication
• Coach and mentor engineering and non-degreed engineering professionals
structured_description.qualifications:
• Bachelor of Science in Engineering from an ABET-accredited program (or Master's degree in engineering)
• 4–6 years of engineering experience for Engineer III level; minimum 6 years for Senior Engineer level OR 5 years with Professional Engineer state registration
• Ability to achieve Unescorted Access and security clearance
• Fit for Duty capability for Emergency Response Organization (ERO) responsibilities including on-call rotation
structured_description.desired:
• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering
• Professional Engineer (PE) registration
• Experience with control systems equipment (analog instrumentation, PLCs, DCS)
• Experience troubleshooting control systems and process instrumentation
• Knowledge of fluid processes, instrument measuring technologies, and installation practices
• Skilled in engineering theories, principles, and design issue research methodologies
• Experience with electrical power systems (Low, Medium, High Voltage)
• Experience with electrical protective relaying and associated components
structured_description.location_details: Harris Nuclear Plant, New Hill, North Carolina. Hybrid work: 2 days remote, 2 days onsite per 4–10 hour workweek after onboarding. ERO callouts with defined response time required; must live within reasonable commute to plant. Industrial environment work required.

structured_description.about: Nuclear Instrumentation & Control (I&C) Design Engineer for Duke Energy's Robinson Nuclear Plant in Hartsville, SC. This position (fillable at Engineer I or Engineer II level based on experience) focuses on electrical and digital control system design, including specifications, design packages, and NRC-compliant cyber security integration for reactor instrumentation and safety systems.
structured_description.responsibilities:
- Perform design engineering for electrical and I&C projects, including digital and software-focused control systems
- Develop design packages, conceptual designs, and specifications for bidding and implementation
- Evaluate design alternatives, conduct design package reviews, and develop setpoints
- Prepare design documentation (calculations, drawings, technical specifications) and coordinate with vendors and A/E firms
- Provide technical support during design implementation and serve as single point of contact for assigned projects
- Ensure NRC cyber security compliance in all digital designs
- Qualify as a Responsible Engineer for modifications and exercise independent technical judgment once qualified
- Support emergency response and storm response operations as assigned
structured_description.qualifications:
- Bachelor of Science in Electrical or Computer Engineering (ABET-accredited) or Master's degree in engineering (ABET-accredited)
- Ability to obtain and maintain unescorted access to nuclear facility (General Employee Training, Radiation Worker Training, Security Clearance, Fitness for Duty)
- Strong oral and written communication skills
- Ability to research engineering issues, evaluate alternatives, and make sound technical recommendations
- Team collaboration skills
- Engineer II level: minimum 2 years related nuclear or power industry work experience
structured_description.desired:
- Current qualification as a Modification Engineer under an INPO-accredited program
- Knowledge of Nuclear Asset Suite for design and work order development
- Familiarity with NRC cyber security regulations (10 CFR Part 73.54)
- Prior qualification credentials and product demonstrations from other utilities
structured_description.location_details: Robinson Nuclear Plant, Hartsville, SC. Position requires unescorted access to secure nuclear facility areas and availability for emergency/storm response support.

structured_description.about: Occupational Health Nurse at Duke Energy nuclear facilities providing first aid case management, regulatory compliance physicals, and occupational health services. structured_description.responsibilities:
- Perform physical examinations for NRC, OSHA, and regulatory compliance; determine type of mandated physicals required
- Assess injuries and illnesses to determine appropriate treatment (first aid, basic life support, treatment or referral)
- Provide first aid care during normal working hours and on-call after-hours to prevent escalation to OSHA recordable events
- Document all medical examinations, tests, consultations, evaluations, and work-related events; maintain confidential employee medical files in compliance with HIPAA and state/federal law
- Make appropriate referrals for employees not medically cleared; obtain physician concurrence on medical clearances as required
- Schedule physical exams and medical tests to meet business needs and regulatory due dates
- Alert Duke Energy WC Coordinator, vendor management, and off-site medical facilities of employee injuries as appropriate
- Function as resource to employees for personal health issues and concerns; refer to external health agencies and EAP as needed
- Provide medical review on Return to Work forms for management
- Conduct health education through written articles, PowerPoint presentations, and active participation in safety meetings
- Perform hands-on ergonomic evaluations and support corporate wellness programs
- Travel as needed to assess employees in assigned Duke Energy locations; willing to travel overnight for emergency deployments (storm duty)
- Provide medical support for special events and training
structured_description.qualifications:
- Associate's degree in Nursing
- Two years of work experience as Occupational Health Nurse OR two years hospital experience
- Valid Registered Nurse license in state of practice
- Basic Life Support (CPR) Certification
- Knowledge of ADA, FMLA, OSHA, and Workers' Compensation laws with ability to make sound medical decisions
- Knowledge of HIPAA requirements and ability to handle confidential medical information appropriately
- Proficiency with computers, email, MS Word, MS Excel, and Occupational Health data programs
- Ability to work independently with minimal supervision
- Excellent people skills and high level of attention to detail

jobs.title: Civil and Environmental Engineer
jobs.description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Civil and Environmental Engineer to join our engineering and deployment team. We are looking to fill this position immediately.

Position Description

Oklo is developing advanced fission power plants to deliver clean, reliable, and affordable energy at scale. As we expand deployment activities, we are looking for a Civil / Environmental Engineer to lead early-stage site development planning and civil infrastructure definition for future Oklo project sites.

In this role, you will own the development of conceptual site layouts, grading and drainage approaches, utility routing concepts, and preliminary civil works packages that support project siting, permitting, estimating, and execution planning. You will work cross-functionally with energy strategy, environmental, construction, operations, and project deployment teams to translate high-level project requirements into practical and buildable site concepts.

This position is ideal for someone who enjoys combining technical engineering judgment with fast-paced project development work and wants to play a foundational role in deploying next-generation clean energy infrastructure.

Specific responsibilities may include:

Develop conceptual and preliminary site layouts for advanced reactor facilities and supporting infrastructure that includes harmonizing development with natural landscape features and ecological functions

Design and develop industrial site layouts that integrate sustainability principles, incorporating natural features (e.g., topography, vegetation, drainage patterns) to optimize environmental performance, resilience, and regulatory compliance

Generate early-stage civil works plans including grading, drainage, access roads, stormwater systems, underground utilities, laydown areas, and construction support facilities

Support site feasibility studies, constructability evaluations, and site selection efforts

Prepare estimates on overburden and spoils generated and cost estimates for civil and site development scopes

Coordinate with environmental, geotechnical, structural, mechanical, electrical, and construction teams to ensure integrated site solutions

Support permitting and environmental review activities, including coordination with local, state, and federal agencies

Interface with external engineering firms, EPC partners, surveyors, and geotechnical consultants

Develop technical specifications, scopes of work, and design criteria for civil engineering activities

Support development of project schedules and execution strategies for site preparation and construction activities

Participate in iterative design reviews and continuously refine site concepts as project requirements evolve

Generate clear technical documentation, reports, drawings, and presentations supporting internal and external stakeholders

Support construction planning, sequencing, and field execution activities as projects mature

 

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, or related discipline

5+ years of relevant engineering experience in industrial, energy, infrastructure, environmental, or site development projects

Experience developing site layouts, grading plans, utility concepts, and civil design packages

Familiarity with civil engineering design tools such as Civil 3D, AutoCAD, GIS platforms, or equivalent

Experience preparing conceptual cost estimates and quantity takeoffs

Understanding of stormwater management, drainage design, and utility coordination

Familiarity with applicable codes, standards, and permitting processes

Ability to travel occasionally to project and development sites

Professional Engineer (PE) license or Engineer in Training (EIT) with expectation of PE certification

 

Bonus Qualifications

Experience with nuclear, industrial, energy, or mission-critical infrastructure projects

Experience supporting environmental permitting or NEPA processes

Familiarity with geotechnical investigations and site characterization activities

Experience coordinating with EPC contractors and construction teams

Experience with construction field engineering or construction management

Knowledge of DOE, NRC, OSHA, EPA, or state environmental regulations

Experience working in startup or highly iterative engineering environments

 

Competencies

We are looking for a Civil / Environmental Engineer that is:

Experienced in site development, land development, industrial facilities, energy infrastructure, or heavy civil projects

Passionate about clean energy and infrastructure deployment

Comfortable owning broad technical scopes in a highly collaborative environment

Excited to work in a fast-paced, highly iterative startup environment

Able to balance conceptual thinking with practical execution details

Willing to think differently and develop creative solutions to infrastructure and site challenges

Comfortable navigating ambiguity and shifting project priorities

Highly organized and capable of managing multiple parallel projects

An excellent communicator capable of presenting technical concepts clearly to multidisciplinary teams

A strong writer capable of producing concise, thoughtful technical documentation

Passionate about integrating technical aspects of site layout with aesthetic and natural features

Understands the importance of balancing technical needs with community acceptance

Motivated by building first-of-a-kind systems and infrastructure

Able to optimize first of a kind designs towards Nth of a kind designs by making valid engineering assumptions, identifying common plant elements, and reducing negative space

 

Who you are:

A startup person: You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that.

Motivated: You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals.

A team-player: Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team.

An excellent communicator: We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator.

Creative: Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day.

Detail-oriented: This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward.

 

About Oklo travel requirements:

Oklo requires remote employees to travel to headquarters (Santa Clara, CA) twice a quarter annually, based on business or team needs, including attendance at team meetings, off-sites, and other company events or gatherings. For the first two weeks of onboarding, employees are required to be in person at headquarters in Santa Clara, CA.

 

About Oklo compensation:

Salary:$130,000-$180,000

Oklo offers flexible time off, equity, competitive pay, 401k, health insurance, FSA, flexible work hours, and other benefits.

Manage progress on external hazards analyses, regulatory submittals, and licensing support.

Develop and maintain regulatory strategy documents, white papers, and briefing materials that articulate the approach to addressing external hazard requirements.

Represent external hazards considerations in cross-functional planning and strategic meetings with internal stakeholders.

Oversee internal external hazards project management systems.

Collaborate with engineering, design, and licensing teams to incorporate hazard analysis results into probabilistic risk assessments, safety evaluations, and licensing deliverables.

Review deliverables from constructors relevant to external hazards.

Coordinate the preparation and review of responses to NRC requests for additional information (RAIs) related to external hazards topics.

Author, edit, and finalize technical reports, regulatory filings, presentations, and licensing documents using modern documentation tools and best practices for clarity and consistency.

Minimum of 3 years of experience performing or evaluating external hazards assessments 

Bachelors, Masters, or PhD in civil engineering, environmental engineering, nuclear engineering, or similar field

Technical expertise in external hazards and their impact on facilities

Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a External Quality Assurance Lead to join our team. 

This is NOT a software quality role. We will not be reviewing applications that are closely related to technical software skillsets. 

Position Description

The External Quality Assurance Lead is responsible for providing senior-level oversight of external suppliers supporting our advanced nuclear reactors and other related projects. This role is responsible for leading nuclear quality audits, qualifying and monitoring suppliers, and ensuring purchased materials, equipment, software, and services conform to applicable quality, regulatory, technical, and procurement requirements.

Specific responsibilities may include:

Serve as a Lead Auditor for external supplier audits, including audit planning, team coordination, checklist development, entrance and exit meetings, evaluation of objective evidence, issuance of audit reports, and verification of corrective-action closure.

Provide guidance and mentoring to audit team members and internal stakeholders on audit practices, supplier oversight expectations, procurement quality controls, and evidence-based assessment methods.

Manage supplier evaluations and qualifications, including initial qualification, requalification, scope changes, technical capability reviews, QA program evaluations, and maintenance of the approved supplier list.

Manage supplier nonconformances, audit findings, corrective-action requests, and supplier performance issues from identification through causal evaluation, corrective action, effectiveness review, and closure.

Develop and maintain the annual and long-range supplier audit and surveillance schedule using risk, safety significance, procurement scope, supplier performance, and project needs.

Plan and perform supplier surveillances, source inspections, witness and hold-point oversight, and performance-based assessments at supplier facilities.

Review supplier quality assurance programs, procedures, records, and implementation for alignment with applicable requirements, including ASME NQA-1, 10 CFR Part 50 Appendix B, procurement quality clauses, and contractual commitments.

Partner with Procurement and Engineering to define and flow down procurement quality requirements, acceptance criteria, documentation requirements, special process requirements, inspection requirements, and applicable Part 21 obligations.

Support evaluation of deviations, defects, counterfeit/fraudulent/suspect items, and supplier-reported issues, including escalation to appropriate internal stakeholders for Part 21 or other reportability screening when applicable.

Ensure supplier documentation and records, such as certificates of conformance, material certifications, inspection records, test reports, calibration records, special process qualifications, and traceability records, are complete and acceptable before use or acceptance.

Oklo is transforming the future of energy, and we’re looking for a Hardware Test Engineer with 4+ years of dedicated experience in testing within regulated industries. In this role, you will develop, execute, and manage test projects—specializing in thermo-hydraulic, materials, and/or mechanical testing—to ensure the highest standards of quality, safety, and compliance. You’ll join a dynamic team where precision meets innovation, shaping testing methodologies that drive towards cheap, abundant, clean energy.

Reporting & Analysis: Compile, analyze, and communicate test data through clear, concise reports that pinpoint performance outcomes, identify potential risks, and offer actionable insights.

Procurement Activities: Manage test procurement processes—coordinate with suppliers and oversee tool, equipment, and material sourcing—to ensure project requirements are met.

Project Management: Oversee testing projects from initiation to completion, collaborating closely with cross-functional teams to maintain project timelines, quality, and regulatory compliance.

Technical Expertise: Proficiency in thermo-hydraulic, materials, and/or mechanical testing methodologies, including setup, data collection, and analysis, ensuring robust and reliable outcomes.

jobs.title: Human Factors Engineer
jobs.description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Human Factors Engineer to join our team.

Position Description

Oklo is seeking a Human Factors Engineer to develop the human factors safety basis for a first-of-a-kind used nuclear fuel (UNF) recycling facility. This individual will own the application of Human Factors Engineering to safety-significant personnel activities. This individual will heavily impact the development of personnel activities, evaluation of personnel activities, design of human-system interfaces, and development of procedures. This individual will foster safety through facilitating correct, and inhibiting wrong, decisions by personnel and by ensuring there exist adequate means for detecting, correcting, and compensating for human error.

Specific responsibilities may include:

Develop the human factors engineering (HFE) strategy, implementation plans, technical bases, and safety basis documentation, including HFE inputs to the integrated safety analysis (ISA), items relied on for safety (IROFS), management measures, and safety program commitments.

Tailor NRC HFE guidance and fuel-cycle-facility review expectations into a practical, graded HFE program appropriate for a first-of-a-kind used nuclear fuel recycling facility.

Evaluate the implementation of human factors engineering best practices in the development of safety-significant personnel activities including actions credited in safety analyses, abnormal event response, maintenance, inspections, surveillance, material handling, and recovery activities.

Lead operating experience reviews, functional requirements analyses, function allocation, task analyses, staffing and qualifications analyses, and human action evaluations across startup, normal operations, shutdown, maintenance, abnormal operations, emergency response, and degraded equipment or interface conditions.

Position Description

The Manager, Supply Chain Systems Transformation is responsible for designing, implementing, and continuously improving the systems, processes, analytics, and operational infrastructure that enable Oklo’s supply chain organization to scale from development activities to fleet deployment.

This role serves as the business owner for supply chain enterprise systems, including Procurement Orchestration, Procure-to-Pay, Supplier Management, Inventory Management, Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), Quality Management Systems (QMS), and future ERP platforms. Working closely with implementation partners, software vendors, Information Technology, and operational stakeholders, this individual will ensure these systems are configured, adopted, and optimized to deliver measurable business value.

The Manager, Supply Chain Systems Transformation operates as a business process architect and internal product manager, translating operational requirements into scalable workflows, system configurations, reporting capabilities, and analytics that support Procurement, Manufacturing, Quality, Engineering, Construction, Finance, and Program teams.

This role also owns the supply chain performance measurement framework, including development of dashboards, KPIs, reporting, and analytics that provide visibility into procurement effectiveness, operational readiness, inventory health, supplier performance, and overall supply chain execution.

This position reports to the Senior Director of Procurement & Supply Chain and may be based in Santa Clara, CA or remotely within the United States.

jobs.title: Mechanical Design Engineer - Fuel Recycling
jobs.description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Mechanical Design Engineer to join our fuel recycling engineering team.

Position Description:

The person in this role is responsible for the design, prototyping, and iterative refinement of production-scale, remotely operated electrochemical molten salt process equipment used in nuclear fuel recycling. This work directly supports Oklo’s mission to close the fuel cycle and enable advanced fission technology deployment.

The systems developed will operate in high-temperature (>500 °C) and high-radiation environments, demanding robust, maintainable designs suitable for automation, remote operation, and long service lifetimes. Day-to-day activities will include mechanical design, testing, and validation of process and mechanical systems that perform reliably in these extreme conditions.

This role will include participation in cross-functional teams focused on facility design, nuclear and electrochemical engineering, instrumentation and controls, automation and robotics, process modeling, quality assurance, and licensing.

Specific responsibilities may include:

Develop and own the mechanical design of process and system components within Oklo’s nuclear fuel recycling facilities.

Design and validate high-temperature (>500 °C) and corrosion-resistant electrochemical process equipment, suitable for operation in high-radiation environments.

Incorporate design-for-automation principles to enable remote handling, inspection, and maintenance of systems and components.

Collaborate cross-functionally with other engineering teams to define design and functional requirements, ensuring compliance with safety regulations and industry standards

Lead and participate in formal design reviews, providing and integrating multidisciplinary technical feedback.

Generate and maintain 3D CAD models, 2D drawings, and bills of materials in controlled PDM/PLM environments.

Prepare clear and traceable engineering documentation, including design rationales, functional requirements, and regulatory submissions.

Collaborate directly with fabrication partners and vendors to refine designs for manufacturability, cost effectiveness, and scalability.

Support equipment prototyping, testing, and commissioning at Oklo’s recycling development and deployment sites.

 

Competencies:

We are looking for a Mechanical Design Engineer that is:

Passionate about clean energy and closing the nuclear fuel cycle.

Proficient in 3D mechanical design (Siemens NX, Solidworks, Creo, etc) with a deep understanding of high-temperature, radiation-tolerant, and industrial process systems.

Experienced or eager to learn about automated and remotely operated systems in nuclear or heavy industrial environments.

Energized by tackling and overcoming complex design challenges in extreme operating conditions.

Passionate about designing for manufacturability, maintainability, and automation.

Comfortable collaborating in multidisciplinary teams with mechanical, controls, and materials engineers.

An optimist at heart, comfortable in a fast-paced, highly iterative startup environment.

Excited to think creatively, critically, and reflectively about the problems they are solving while not leaning only on what has been done before 

Willing to propose novel and creative solutions to technical problems

An excellent communicator, both verbally and in writing—able to produce clear, modern, and compelling technical documentation.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s or higher degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field (e.g., Materials or Nuclear Engineering).

5-10 years of experience demonstrating success taking mechanical systems from concept through detailed design, analysis, fabrication, and deployment.

Experience with custom mechanical design for equipment used in high-temperature or heavy industrial applications (e.g. nuclear, petrochemical, or mining industries).

Expert-level proficiency with CAD software (e.g., Siemens NX, CATIA, SolidWorks), including 3D model generation and 2D fabrication drawings.

Broad familiarity with engineering principles and strong systems engineering intuition.

Working knowledge of material selection, particularly high-temperature alloys and corrosion-resistant metals, along with related manufacturing and joining techniques.

Bonus Qualifications:

Experience with electrochemical manufacturing processes such as electroplating, electrowinning, or pyroprocessing.

Experience designing equipment for high (>500 °C) temperature operation or corrosive molten salt environments.

Experience designing for radiation tolerance or remote maintenance in nuclear or space systems.

Familiarity with design for automation, including integration with robotics and control systems for “lights-out” operations.

Experience designing heavy industrial equipment or pilot-scale systems with high reliability and extended maintenance intervals.

Experience with ANSYS or similar FEA/CFD simulation software for structural and thermal analysis.

Knowledge of GD&T and design for manufacturability best practices.

Experience with balance of plant facility design and integration with automated process systems.

Experience in commercial or governmental nuclear projects.

Who you are:

A startup person: You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that.

Motivated: You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals.

A team-player: Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team.

An excellent communicator: We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator.

Creative: Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day.

Detail-oriented: This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Even excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward.

 

About Oklo compensation:

Salary: $80,000-$155,000

Oklo offers flexible time off, equity, competitive pay, 401k, health insurance, FSA, flexible work hours, and other benefits.

We are looking to fill this position immediately!

jobs.title: Network Systems Technician
jobs.description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Network Systems Technician to join our team.

Position Description

Oklo, Inc. is seeking a skilled and hands-on Network Systems Technician to support and maintain the company’s network infrastructure, endpoint connectivity, and on-site IT systems. This role is focused on ensuring reliable, secure, and high-performing network and systems operations across Oklo’s offices, labs, and collaboration spaces.

The Network Systems Technician will work closely with the IT/Cyber team to support daily operations, troubleshoot network and system issues, and assist with infrastructure upgrades in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys being close to the hardware, solving real-world connectivity problems, and providing excellent technical support to users.

This is an on-site position in Santa Clara, CA. 

Specific responsibilities may include:

Network & Connectivity Support

Support and maintain wired and wireless network infrastructure, including switches, access points, firewalls, and cabling

Troubleshoot network connectivity issues across user endpoints, conference rooms, labs, and office environments

Assist with network configuration tasks such as VLANs, DNS, DHCP, and IP addressing

Support VPN and secure remote access solutions in coordination with the IT/Cyber team

Systems & Endpoint Support

Provide hands-on support for user endpoints running macOS, Ubuntu/Linux, and Windows

Assist with provisioning, setup, and maintenance of endpoint devices and peripherals

Support basic server and virtualization environments (e.g., VMware) as needed

Manage user access and device connectivity using tools such as JumpCloud, Jamf, Intune, or equivalent platforms

A/V and On-Site Technology Support

Support audio/visual systems in conference rooms and collaboration spaces, including setup, testing, and troubleshooting

Ensure reliable network and system connectivity for meetings, presentations, and company events

Coordinate with on-site staff to support day-to-day IT and A/V needs

Security & Compliance Support

Implement and follow IT and network security best practices, including patching, secure configurations, and access controls

Assist with enforcing data protection and export-controlled data handling requirements (e.g., 10 CFR Part 810)

Support backup, recovery, and basic monitoring solutions for network-connected systems

Collaboration & Continuous Improvement

Work closely with the IT/Cyber team to support infrastructure improvements and new technology deployments

Assist with network and systems upgrades, refreshes, and expansions

Document network diagrams, configurations, procedures, and troubleshooting steps

Identify recurring issues and propose practical improvements to enhance reliability and user experience

Minimum Qualifications:

2+ years of experience in a Network Technician, IT Support, Systems Technician, or similar role

Networking or IT certifications such as CompTIA Network+, A+, Security+, CCNA or equivalent

Hands-on experience supporting network infrastructure and endpoint connectivity

Working knowledge of macOS, Linux (Ubuntu), and Windows operating systems

Experience supporting A/V systems and on-site IT environments

Must be considered a “U.S. Person” under 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)

Must be local to Santa Clara, CA and able to provide on-site support

Bonus Qualifications:

Experience with VMware or basic virtualization concepts

Familiarity with regulatory or compliance-driven environments (e.g., NIST, DOE, export controls)

Experience using scripting or automation tools to streamline IT or network operations

Competencies

We are looking for a Network Systems Technician who:

Has strong troubleshooting skills across networking, endpoints, and on-site systems

Understands networking fundamentals such as DNS, DHCP, VLANs, routing, and switching

Is comfortable working with macOS, Linux (Ubuntu), and Windows systems

Has experience with enterprise IT and networking tools (e.g., JumpCloud, Meraki, Palo Alto, or similar)

Is hands-on, detail-oriented, and comfortable working directly with hardware and users

Communicates technical information clearly and effectively to non-technical audiences

Can manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced startup environment

Is passionate about clean energy and Oklo’s mission to make advanced fission a reality

Who you are:

A startup person: You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that.

Motivated: You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals.

A team-player: Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team.

An excellent communicator: We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator.

Creative: Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day.

Detail-oriented: This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward.

 

About Oklo travel requirements:

Oklo requires remote employees to travel to headquarters (Santa Clara, CA) twice a quarter annually, based on business or team needs, including attendance at team meetings, off-sites, and other company events or gatherings. For the first two weeks of onboarding, employees are required to be in person at headquarters in Santa Clara, CA.

 

About Oklo compensation:

Salary: $60,000-$80,000

Oklo offers flexible time off, equity, competitive pay, 401k, health insurance, FSA, flexible work hours, and other benefits.

 

This position may involve access to information subject to U.S. export control laws. Only applicants who meet the definition of a U.S. person under applicable laws may be eligible.

Oklo is also developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. National Laboratories.

Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Radiation Safety Officer (RSO) to join our team. 

This position will be on-site in Idaho Falls, Idaho.

Position Description

Oklo Isotopes is building scalable U.S. radioisotope production capabilities in facilities dedicated to producing essential isotopes for healthcare, space, industry, research, and defense applications. In February 2026, Oklo’s Idaho Radioisotopes Laboratory (IRL) located in Idaho Falls received its Material Possession License from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to take a leading role in the manufacturing and distribution of beneficial radioisotopes in the U.S.

We are seeking a Radiation Safety Officer (RSO) to serve as the technical authority for radiation protection activities at the IRL. This role is designed for an experienced Certified Health Physicist (CHP) or an equivalently seasoned radiation protection professional who brings strong technical judgment, operational leadership, and deep expertise in radiation safety program implementation.

The Radiation Safety Officer owns the Radiation Protection Program for IRL and is responsible for ensuring safe, compliant, and efficient radiological operations in support of isotope production, laboratory operations, radioactive material handling, and facility readiness activities. This role combines strategic program leadership with hands-on operational engagement and provides significant influence over facility operations, licensing activities, operational readiness, and long-term safety culture.

Specific responsibilities may include:

Serve as the designated Radiation Safety Officer with technical authority and accountability for the IRL Radiation Protection Program in accordance with NRC requirements, applicable State regulations, and site procedures.

Establish, maintain, and enforce radiation protection standards, radiological controls, and operational procedures using sound health physics principles.

Provide technical oversight and guidance for radioactive material handling, isotope production activities, contamination controls, radioactive waste management, and radiological work planning.

Lead, mentor, and develop radiation protection personnel, technicians, and operational staff to maintain strong field execution and radiological safety culture.

Perform and oversee complex radiological evaluations including shielding analyses, dose assessments, contamination control strategies, ALARA planning, and radiological work reviews.

Integrate radiation protection requirements into facility modifications, operational procedures, commissioning activities, and infrastructure upgrades.

Serve as the primary technical interface with regulatory authorities during inspections, audits, licensing activities, and regulatory communications.

Help prepare, review, and approve regulatory documentation, license amendments, corrective action plans, radiological procedures, and radiation safety training programs.

Lead investigations of radiological events, abnormal occurrences, and operational issues including root cause analysis and corrective action development.

Promote operational excellence, procedural compliance, industrial safety, and a strong nuclear safety culture.

Strong working knowledge of NRC regulations, radiation protection principles, ALARA practices, contamination controls, and radiological work planning.

Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with regulators, senior leadership, and multidisciplinary technical teams.

Strong technical writing, organizational, problem-solving, and operational decision-making skills.

Certified Health Physicist (CHP) strongly preferred.

Experience supporting radioisotope production facilities, hot cell operations, gloveboxes, or nuclear laboratory environments.

Experience supporting startup, commissioning, or operational readiness activities.

jobs.description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Radioactive Waste Handling Engineer to join our Fuel Recycling Team.

 

Position Description

The Radioactive Waste Handling Engineer is responsible for designing and implementing compliant, safe, and effective shipping and storage solutions for nuclear materials ranging from byproduct to Class A through high-level waste (HLW) items. This role will play a critical part in ensuring regulatory compliance, operational excellence, and technical rigor in nuclear waste management.

In this position, you will

Collaborate with internal teams, regulators, and external partners to design, implement, and oversee waste storage programs for the Oklo Fuel Recycling Team.

Design, analyze, and implement waste storage systems and packaging that comply with NRC regulations and industry standards.

Manage contracts with licensed disposal facilities, transporters, and shippers to ensure safe and compliant waste disposition.

 

Specific responsibilities may include:

Performing engineering analyses of waste package performance (e.g., chemical, thermal, radiological, etc.) to support the development of the safety case for the Oklo Fuel Recycling Facility.

Collaborating cross-functionally with operations, engineering, and licensing teams to integrate waste storage requirements into facility and program designs.

Facilitating design of storage facilities and processes to ensure regulatory compliance with 10 CFR Part 72.

Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Senior Electrical Engineer to join our team. 

Position Description

In this role, you will own the design, development, integration, and validation of electrical systems supporting a nuclear fuel recycling facility. This is a first-of-a-kind (FOAK) facility, and this role requires ownership across the full lifecycle from early concept development through detailed design, construction, commissioning, and operations.

This role includes close collaboration with cross-functional teams focused on facility design, process engineering, controls engineering, equipment design, and licensing.

Lead the design and implementation of facility electrical systems from concept through commissioning

Design and specify high-, medium-, and low-voltage power distribution systems

Define system architecture, including redundancy, backup power, and safety strategies

Perform and review power system studies (load flow, short-circuit, coordination)

Generate and review electrical documentation (single-line diagrams, load lists, specifications, cable schedules)

Lead integration with control systems (PLC/DCS/HMI)

Develop grounding, bonding, and lightning protection strategies

Support procurement, installation, and commissioning activities

Collaborate on facility layout, constructability, and maintainability

Generate technical documentation supporting regulatory and licensing efforts

Serve as the electrical technical lead across lifecycle stages

Minimum Qualifications:

Degree in Electrical Engineering or related field

10+ years of experience designing and deploying industrial or facility-scale electrical systems

Demonstrated ownership of electrical system design through multiple project phases (concept through commissioning)

Experience in nuclear, fuel cycle, or similarly regulated industrial environments

Deep experience in power systems design (switchgear, transformers, protection systems)

Commissioning and startup experience in complex facilities

Motivated by building, and getting technology deployed

Position Description

As a Senior Mechanical Design Engineer at Oklo, you will play a central role in designing the critical hardware that enables our advanced fast reactors to operate safely and reliably. This includes technical ownership of large, multi-component weldments and assemblies that comprise the reactor module within our Aurora powerhouses—ranging from the reactor vessel to various internal support structures and primary coolant flow elements. You will be responsible for advancing these components from conceptual design through detailed design and fabrication readiness, ensuring that every element is engineered for performance, manufacturability, industrial Code compliance, and integration into Oklo’s broader reactor system. Your work will require deep engagement with cross-functional teams including structural analysts, systems engineers, materials experts, and external design and fabrication partners.

This is a high-responsibility role at the heart of our flagship product. Success in this position requires producing quality mechanical solutions in a fast-paced, startup environment where technical excellence and a collaborative mindset are equally valued.

Develop and own the design of complex mechanical components and subsystems within the reactor module

Use CAD tools to translate functional requirements into robust designs that meet structural, thermal, and integration constraints

Conduct and participate in design reviews, providing and receiving technical feedback

Rigorously evaluate mechanical designs to identify deficiencies and proactively propose and implement solutions

Generate and maintain detailed 3D CAD models, 2D drawings, and bills of materials using controlled processes in PDM/PLM systems

Coordinate closely with analysis teams to guide and interpret thermal, structural, fatigue, and safety analyses in support of design validation

Perform detailed manufacturability reviews, tolerance studies, and DFM/DFA assessments to prepare components for fabrication and assembly

Create and maintain clear, well-written engineering documentation, including design rationales, functional requirements, reviews of historical designs, and detailed explanations of system architecture and performance

Work closely with fabrication partners to refine designs for cost-effective and practical production

This role will be a key member of the Fuels project teams and will partner closely with the Project Manager, Project Sponsor and Fuels’ business leaders to ensure rigorous cost control, schedule integration, financial transparency, and performance accountability throughout the project lifecycle.

This role interfaces with the EPC and other vendors, reviewing reporting, participating in regular updates, and constructively challenging cost and progress assumptions. 

The Project Controller will work in close coordination with the Capital Cost Management and the Planning and Scheduling team to ensure project-level cost tracking, reporting, and forecasting remain aligned with the project plan, physical progress as well as with established cost frameworks, breakdown structures, and governance standards.

This role reports into the Sr. Director of Project Budgeting and Controls with day-to-day integration within project teams.

Specific responsibilities may include:

Forecasting and EAC Ownership: Develop and maintain independent cost-to-complete and Estimate at Completion (EAC) positions, ensuring forecasts reflect financial reality and risk exposure. Cost Control and Tracking: Provide trusted reporting, trending, and variance analyses of commitments and actual expenditures compared to project budgets. 

Project Performance Assessment: Lead cost and schedule integration to assess project performance, including the financial impacts of schedule changes and drive transparency between progress and cost performance. 

Risk and Performance Management: Identify and quantify cost and schedule risk. Maintain independent, data-informed judgement of project performance and escalate concerns around forecast integrity and compliance. Monitor contingency utilization and change order trends. 

Reporting & Insights: Own monthly project financial reporting packages and executive-ready project narratives. Support the preparation of materials for senior leadership reviews as required.

Vendor and Contract Performance Oversight: Review and audit contractor and vendor cost reports and validate progress against contractual milestones, physical progress and schedule status. Governance and Framework Alignment: Ensure project-level cost tracking aligns with standardized methodologies and governance frameworks established through partnership with the Capital Cost Management team. Maintain and enforce cost discipline and reporting consistency across project teams.

Clear and concise communication skills

Startup or high-growth company experience

jobs.title: Software Lifecycle Specialist
jobs.description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Software Lifecycle Specialist to join our team. 

Position Description

This role will be focused on strengthening our software development lifecycle, ensuring high-quality delivery, and maintaining compliance with internal and regulatory standards. We support a variety of internal “customers” and establish the processes, tooling structures, and governance frameworks that allow engineering teams to execute effectively and transparently. Oklo is a fast- moving startup, and we are actively formalizing lifecycle rigor while preserving engineering velocity. You will have the opportunity to shape how software is scoped, tracked, governed, and released across the company. A nuclear background is not required, but strong systems thinking, attention to detail, a proactive mindset, and a sense of curiosity about the domain are all essential in this role.

 

Specific responsibilities may include:

Members of the Systems Enablement team help align tooling, governance, and execution across engineering domains. In this role you might:

Define and maintain software lifecycle standards, templates, and workflows across GitLab and Jira.

Establish and enforce traceability between requirements, design artifacts, code, testing, and validation activities.

Partner with engineers to ensure proper scoping, backlog hygiene, and milestone alignment.

Define change control and configuration management expectations in collaboration with DevOps/Engineering Infrastructure.

Support audit readiness by ensuring lifecycle documentation and records are complete and reproducible.

Define lifecycle standards including Definition of Done expectations and release controls.

Build reporting and dashboards that provide visibility into lifecycle health, risk, and delivery status.

Identify gaps in the software lifecycle and improve engineering workflows.

Translate compliance requirements into practical, implementable engineering workflows.

Evaluate and recommend tooling improvements that strengthen lifecycle integrity without introducing unnecessary process overhead.

 

Minimum Qualifications:

Weʼd like to see a clear track record of the following, based on your past roles and experience: 

Bachelorʼs degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent industry experience.

5+ years of experience in software development, DevOps, technical program management, software quality, or systems engineering.

Experience working in regulated or compliance-driven environments.

Strong understanding of software development lifecycle concepts including requirements traceability, version control, CI/CD, configuration management, validation, and release control.

Experience working with Jira or similar issue tracking systems in a structured, milestone-driven environment.

Experience documenting processes clearly and unambiguously.

Strong cross-functional communication skills.

Comfort operating in ambiguous environments and building structure where none exists.

 

Bonus Qualifications: 

Prior experience with our stack and tools is helpful, but not required:

Experience supporting NQA-1, ISO 9001, NIST, or similar regulatory or compliance frameworks.

Experience with GitLab, especially GitLab CI/CD and repository governance controls.

Experience defining or auditing SDLC frameworks.

Experience building dashboards or lifecycle reporting tools.

Experience supporting engineering organizations with hardware, simulation, or embedded systems.

Familiarity with CAD or PLM lifecycle controls.

Experience writing or maintaining work instructions and formal procedures.

Experience with secure software development lifecycle frameworks such as CSSLP or similar certifications.

 

Who you are:

A startup person: You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that.

Motivated: You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals.

A team-player: Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team.

An excellent communicator: We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator.

Creative: Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day.

Detail-oriented: This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward.

As part of the Systems Enablement team, you will help evaluate, onboard, integrate, and manage the engineering tools and platforms that enable teams across Oklo to design, simulate, and deliver advanced fission power technology. jobs.title: Construction Project Coordinator
jobs.description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Construction Project Coordinator to support our Aurora-INL EPC Project Management team.

Position Description

The Construction Project Coordinator supports the planning, coordination, execution, and closeout of EPC and capital construction activities for the Aurora-INL project under the supervision of project management, construction management, and project controls personnel. This role is responsible for helping organize field activities, project communications, documentation, schedules, action items, procurement support, and construction deliverables throughout the project lifecycle.

The Construction Project Coordinator helps ensure project work is coordinated, documented, and executed in accordance with Oklo standards, project requirements, contractual obligations, quality assurance expectations, safety requirements, and applicable site and regulatory requirements.

This position serves as a key coordination point between Oklo, EPC contractors, vendors, subcontractors, consultants, and internal stakeholders including Engineering, Procurement, Construction, Project Controls, Quality Assurance, Document Control, Safety, Security, and Records Management teams.

Success in this role requires strong organizational discipline, attention to detail, field awareness, sound judgment, and the ability to proactively identify and escalate coordination risks before they affect safety, quality, cost, schedule, or project milestones.

Specific responsibilities may include:

Support day-to-day coordination of construction project activities for Aurora-INL, including meeting preparation, action-item tracking, field coordination, schedule updates, and project reporting. 

Assist project managers, construction managers, superintendents, field engineers, and project controls personnel with coordination of work packages, project priorities, site logistics, and execution readiness. 

Track open actions, constraints, permits, inspections, material needs, vendor deliverables, subcontractor activities, field issues, and upcoming milestones. 

Prepare and maintain project logs, trackers, dashboards, meeting minutes, decision logs, issue logs, and status reports in support of construction execution. 

Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to support timely resolution of RFIs, submittals, technical questions, change items, nonconformances, and field clarification needs. 

Support schedule coordination by collecting progress updates, verifying status information, identifying potential delays, and helping escalate items that may impact critical-path work.

jobs.title: Mechanical Analyst Engineer
jobs.description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a passionate, highly analytical, and detail-oriented Mechanical Analyst Engineer to join our engineering team.

Position Description:

Mechanical Analyst Engineers at Oklo are responsible for the analysis of mechanical components as part of the power plant design. This role is ideal for a mechanical engineer who thrives on solving complex problems through first-principles thinking, rapid iteration hand calculations, and finite element analysis (FEA) when the project requires. You will play a critical role in the progression and optimization of mechanical designs, working closely with design, manufacturing, and testing teams as well as coordinating with external vendors for additional analysis support.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate a strong foundation in fundamental mechanics and strength of materials, with additional expertise in areas such as dynamics, creep, fatigue, and heat transfer. A key aspect of this role includes producing clear, traceable, and reviewable documentation of analytical work, and using your results to recommend design changes or other next steps. You will also contribute to the development and maintenance of in-house analysis methodologies and best practices to support consistency, scalability, and knowledge sharing across the engineering team.

Specific responsibilities may include:

Perform rigorous mechanical analyses across all levels of fidelity, from hand calculations and textbook formulas to highly detailed Finite Element Analysis (FEA)

Evaluate structural performance for stress, creep, fatigue, vibration, temperature limits, and other failure modes

Interpret and apply relevant engineering standards and codes (e.g., ASME, ASCE, AISC) to establish appropriate design limits and acceptance criteria

Develop clear, concise, and technically sound documentation of engineering methodologies, analysis results, and design justifications

Summarize mechanical analysis results in written documents and presentation slides, translating complex data into concise summaries of key findings (e.g., peak stresses, safety margins) and actionable design revision recommendations, and present those results to management and various stakeholders

Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including design, manufacturing, quality, and test engineering to drive design decisions and ensure robust product development

Support the creation and refinement of product requirements

Plan and execute validation and verification activities, including designing and overseeing physical test programs to validate engineering assumptions and design requirements

Competencies:

Passionate about advancing clean energy technologies, with a strong belief in the potential of next-generation fission

Well-versed in structural mechanics, design principles, and analytical methods—across both simulation and practical applications

Eager to contribute to a high-performing engineering team, open to feedback, and committed to continuous technical growth

Quick to learn and unafraid to question assumptions—ready to explore unconventional approaches to complex challenges

Comfortable navigating the pace, ambiguity, and evolution of an innovative startup environment

Brings a thoughtful, systems-level perspective to mechanical problems—balancing creativity, rigor, and first-principles thinking

Communicates technical analyses clearly and concisely, with strong writing skills and a modern, active voice

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s or higher degree in a relevant engineering discipline (e.g., mechanical, aerospace, materials)

4+ years of industry experience performing mechanical or structural analysis within sectors such as energy, aerospace, automotive, defense, industrial machinery, or advanced manufacturing

Proven experience in structural analysis using FEA tools (e.g., Ansys, Abaqus, COMSOL)

Demonstrated ability to write comprehensive technical documentation and reports

Excellent communication and collaboration skills in a multidisciplinary engineering environment

Master's or PhD in engineering

Strong programming skills for automating analysis workflows—preferably Python, with good software development practices

Familiarity with the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code

Section III, Division 1 or 5

Section VIII, Division 2

Nuclear-specific code cases

Experience developing and managing product requirements and associated test and verification plans

Familiarity with configuration management and version control systems (e.g., Git, SVN, etc.)

A startup person: You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that.

Motivated: You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals.

A team-player: Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team.

An excellent communicator: We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator.

Creative: Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day.

Detail-oriented: This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward.
