jobs.description: Job Title: Remote Fleet Operator, RFO Sr - RFO Sr. Lead Work Place Flexibility: Onsite Legal Entity: Entergy Services, LLC At Entergy, we’ve been planning for the future for more than 100 years. We’ve experienced a lot of change, generating power first from sawdust to splitting atoms, harnessing sunlight, and using abundant, clean, and efficient natural gas. We are leading the clean energy transformation for the utility industry and continue to explore alternative technologies. We are on the verge of a monumental technology convergence, where reality swiftly catches up to possibility. The utility of the future does much more than keep the lights on and the gas flowing. It’s knowledgeable and skillful workforce will solve challenges and fuel a brighter, smarter, cleaner, and more prosperous future for everyone. Having the lowest retail electricity rates of any utility in the United States drives economic growth within Entergy’s region, a key ingredient to sustained growth for any utility. We also believe a diverse workforce committed to personal and professional growth is critical to our success. We place a high priority on developing talent to meet current and future needs, giving employees opportunities to grow their careers their way. We’ve committed over the next three decades to reduce our carbon emissions from our operations to net-zero by 2050. Entergy’s Power Generation group operates a fleet of more than 30 owned, leased, or operated natural gas, coal, oil, hydro and solar plants, with a total engineering capacity exceeding 20,000 megawatts. Entergy continues to build or acquire megawatts from new hydrogen capable natural gas units, solar, wind and other technologies to complement its existing megawatts of nuclear, natural gas, coal, oil, hydroelectric, and solar facilities. JOB SUMMARY/PURPOSE: The RFO is part of a team that centrally monitors Entergy’s regulated Power Generation resources’ fleet-wide performance, maintenance, and operations in a “co-location” workspace with the SPO’s EMO generation dispatcher and performance/equipment health monitoring groups. The RFO will operate and maintain systems associated with various fleet assets such as Combustion Turbine Generator (CTG), Reciprocating Internal Combustion Engines (RICE) and renewables facilities while demonstrating safety awareness that will continuously improve performance through the use and strict adherence to procedures and processes. As the new fleet of CCCT’s grows, the RFO will complement the plant commissioning teams to help and gain experience on the Mitsubishi JAC and STG machines. Maintain regulatory compliance and be proactive in supporting responses to all agencies audits to avoid reportable violations. Facilitate and participate in job briefings, shift-turn overs, and safety meetings. Be responsible for NERC/CIP compliance associated with Asset Strategy & Operations functions. Promotes and ensures a safe work environment, including use of Human Performance tools. Operates with a continuous improvement and commercial mindset while prioritizing safety and asset protection over production. Mentors and provides training to develop other remote operators in the operations training progression plan. Performs startup and shutdown functions of turbine, generator and associated equipment as required per instructions from the EMO, LBA & MISO. Works with (EMO) and plant staff to maximize plant production, scheduling unit testing, scheduling planned outages, communicate operational issues and outage return to service. Develops procedures, checklists, and performance measures to monitor process controls to ensure that all operations and regulatory requirements are fulfilled. Develops, implements, and maintains a high standard of performance using operational procedures, operations rounds/trending, shift turnover, protection system functionality etc. Complies with system critical conditions, suspending testing, maintenance, surveillance, equipment swaps and other activities upon issuance of conservative operations or max generation notices from the ISO, LBA, or TCC. Track problems and issues to resolution, including participation in root cause analysis process. Provide real time guidance to Entergy dispatch group to optimize unit commitments and operation throughout the fleet. Routinely review the Tier 1 and Tier 2 instrument lists and assist the plants to resolve issues related to those lists. Drive the alarm management program to minimize nuisance alarms for remotely operated sites. Prepare and provide routine reports on unit performance and equipment condition to plants and management. Assist in the identification, evaluation and implementation of new processes or technology in support of Power Generation key initiatives, such as fuel efficiency, enhanced monitoring, and remote unit operation. Work with reliability analysts/engineers to capture and quantify avoided costs to express the value of the team's activities. JOB SUMMARY/PURPOSE The Lead, SC Standards & Processes–Procurement reports to the Manager, Category Management (Knowledge & Process Excellence), and often works closely with various leaders across the enterprise. This is a Senior Staff position which designs, develops, composes, and administers the standards, procedures and processes that guide the organization’s standard way of working related to Procurement. The position will work closely with all procurement and supply chain departments to ensure that processes are well documented, readily available, and effective. For the purposes of this role scope does not include Sourcing; the plan, strategy, source and perform of the Sourcing, Negotiating or Contracting, but it shall include Materials activities which correlate with Procurement within the end-to-end process of Materials Management. The position shall work very closely with the respective Leads for Supply Chain Standards & Processes for both Sourcing and Materials. The lead will provide expertise in leading and developing standard procedures and processes related to Procurement activities such as purchase-to-pay, operational purchasing, category purchasing, contract purchasing, services, PO and invoice management & reconciliation. The lead will also provide other coordination and related deliverables that enable effective, informed, and valuable interaction with stakeholders, and application where applicable with supply chain systems and solutions. The position delivers value to the company by developing streamlined procedures and consistency, supporting ongoing process improvement and enabling world class performance through ensuring procurement and supply chain’s standard methods of working for Procurement. Actively promote strong safety behaviors, utilizing key tools such as Close Call / Good Catch - in addition to proactive field and office visits to review standards and behaviors. Monitors and influences suppliers and other stakeholders to proactively identify safety concerns. Levers Procurement best practices to support supply chain safety manager in services of the enterprise. Develop and administer clear, consistent, well-defined standards, processes and procedures related to Procurement activities across P&SC functions which are easily understood by those who utilize them. Interpret company policies, processes and procedures to ensure adherence and consistency within the procurement and supply chain function. Define process performance and compliance KPI’s and metrics Partner with stakeholders to define, set, and achieve departmental goals that support the procurement and supply chain strategy and overall organizational goals for technology business services and procurement & supply chain. Partner with suppliers to define, set, and achieve departmental goals that support the procurement and supply chain strategy and overall organizational goals for technology business services and procurement & supply chain. Maintain healthy, positive, and valuable stakeholder relationships within the procurement and supply chain organization and with its customers and suppliers. Mentor and coach staff members, and support the broader talent development activities within the supply chain management organization. Responsible for understanding and administering Procurement and Supply Chain policies and procedures. At all times, operate with highest ethical standards and in full compliance with internal controls, policies, procedures, regulations and laws. jobs.description: Job Title: Senior Manager, Risk and Reliabilty Work Place Flexibility: Onsite Legal Entity: Entergy Louisiana, LLC Job Summary/Purpose The Senior Manager, Risk & Reliability provides strategic direction for the organizations focused on identifying and mitigating risks associated with work execution that may compromise the reliable operation of the transmission system while ensuring holistic support and direction are taken on equipment issues. This role also leads and develops a team of engineers responsible for maintenance engineering, project management support, operations engineering, and emergency restoration activities across transmission and distribution assets. This critical position serves a cross-functional role in driving operational excellence for transmission protection devices and distribution electronic devices, inclusive of all associated processes, supporting all 81 Networks, 21 Grids, and all Capital Projects. Provides technical guidance and direction to a group of SMEs who provide technical support to all Power Delivery Construction and Grid teams, along with Power Generation and Nuclear BUs on the technical aspects of transmission equipment. Influences and sets the structure for organizational adherence to multiple NERC standards. Job Duties/Responsibilities 1. Challenges the transmission organization to apply consistent risk control processes to Capital Projects and Maintenance activities across the transmission system ensuring Bulk Electric System (BES) Reliability. Oversees the development of procedures, performance metrics and training materials to support the adoption of consistent risk control processes in all transmission functions. Collaborates cross-functionally to influence and integrate a risk control mindset into the culture of the entire Power Delivery organization. 2. Collaborate with key stakeholders across the organization including the Transmission Grids, Capital Projects, Commissioning, Project Management, Control Centers, AM Strategy, Design Engineering, Industrial Accounts, and Distribution Networks to ensure quality technical support is provided timely and alignment on deliverables is achieved. Bring awareness to systemwide deficiencies, lead cross-functional efforts, present strategic solutions, and align organizational initiatives to close gaps. 3. Provide strategic oversight of the organization responsible for reviewing and challenging field execution plans through a risk mitigation lens while determining execution readiness of certain capital and maintenance projects and tasks. Provides recommendations for modifying execution plans to minimize and/or eliminate risk. Participate in project team meetings to discuss risk profiles in early development stages of proposed projects. 4. Collaborate with nuclear leadership to ensure alignment of approach in mitigating risk to Entergy’s nuclear generating facilities for both planned and emergent work. Serve as a liaison to Nuclear for Power Delivery on all nuclear procedures and agreements pertaining to transmission. 5. Responsible system owner of NERC standards PRC-004 and PRC-002, while supporting sections of NERC standards TPL-001, PRC-005, 006, 012, 023, 026, 027, CIP-014, and NUC-001. Drives organizational knowledge and adherence to internal procedures and NERC standards. 6. Facilitate technical support with around the clock availability, for all transmission protection and control equipment, transmission line, and substation physical equipment issues, including the development of emergency relay settings. Provides mutual support for transmission type equipment, owned by Nuclear and Power Generation. 7. Provides guidance and direction to the team responsible for developing settings for all Distribution electronic devices across all 81 Networks. Drives initiatives and strategic direction of the Power Delivery organization to reduce customer interruptions through the deployment and maintenance of electronic distribution devices. This team participates in all capital projects, supporting equipment failures, emergency conditions, and troubleshooting activities associated with these devices. 8. Serves in the Incident Command Structure during major events as a leader providing strategic direction and coordination in the system planning section. 9. Serves as a change agent to drive innovation and a culture of continuous improvement through increased utilization of technology and the mindset of performance optimization while improving reliability, customer service, and reducing cost. 10. Able to understand and present complex technical topics with simplification and easy to understand language to audiences ranging from SVP to individual contributors to external industrial customers. Seeks alignment with vice presidents to influence and drive organizational improvements. Minimum Requirements Minimum education required of the position Bachelor’s degree in engineering required. Electrical Engineering preferred. Minimum experience required of the position 8 years of engineering and/or operational experience required with at least 3 years preferred in transmission grid, capital construction or design engineering and 5 years of progressive supervisory experience in Engineering or Grid Operations. Minimum knowledge, skills, and abilities required of the position •Engaged leaders with demonstrated accomplishments of leading and influencing across organizations. • Demonstrated understanding of design engineering, construction, and maintenance practices, procedures, processes, and NERC standards. • Understanding of the project life-cycle process for Distribution projects. • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple groups simultaneously. • Proven leadership skills with demonstrated experience leading and developing high performing teams. • Demonstrated understanding of risk management concepts. • Strong ability to cope with complexities and drive for change in a highly matrixed organization. • Excellent written and verbal interpersonal skills. • Highly organized. • Self-starter with the ability to work individually, within a team, and partner with external stakeholders. • Strong customer orientation. jobs.description: Job Title: Manager, Materials Procurement Work Place Flexibility: Hybrid Legal Entity: Entergy Services, LLC JOB SUMMARY/PURPOSE This position is responsible for managing the Material Procurement operations team that supplies Entergy’s Power Generation plants. The Materials Procurement operations organization is responsible for procurement and management of safety related and non-safety related material. This position serves as a lead team member of our Procurement & Supply Chain (P&SC) team and the group interfaces with all plant departments including Maintenance, Production, Engineering, Operations, Chemistry, and Project Management, Legal, Taxes, Compliance & others, supporting work management, outage and on-line planning preparation and execution of work. The manager position is key in providing governance and oversight of all aspects of the materials procurement processes supporting the organization to improve plant performance and equipment reliability ensuring compliance with applicable quality and regulatory requirements. This position manages multiple and sometimes conflicting priorities and ensures the organization has a culture of being proactively engaged, anticipating material needs, solutions and improvement opportunities. The Manager, Materials Procurement reports to the Senior Manager, Strategic Procurement. JOB DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES Safety/Human Performance: Ensure the Team always puts safety first. Actively promote strong safety behaviors, utilizing key tools such as Close Call /Good Catch in addition to proactive field visits to review standards and behaviors. Monitoring and influencing Suppliers to proactively identify any safety concerns. Materials and Services Procurement: Accountable for excellence in executing procurement of materials services. Drives toward full optimization and utilization of the tiered procurement model and leveraging of Entergy’s full spending power through effective engagement with category management, and the plant contract specialist teams. Leadership: Manage a team of procurement specialists focused on material procurement. Act on behalf of P&SC leadership, as required. Outage Support: Provide support for emergencies, backshift and outage support as required. Deliver effective communications between plant management and the procurement staff for emergent and outage priorities. Support the Incident Response Organization and associated activities. Performance Management: Establish departmental objectives and standards of performance in accordance with defined P&SC objectives and Power Generation site expectations. Actively seek and solicit ideas from staff for continuous improvement. Partnership: Accountable for establishing and maintaining healthy and positive stakeholder relationships. This activity includes establishing cross-functional and cross-sector teams with key stakeholders and helping create multi-year demand plans with integrated supply chain solutions. People Leadership: Accountable for leverage of P&SC’s Talent Management Strategy to assure the right P&SC talent is recruited, developed, retained, and deployed in line with key business priorities. Mentor and coach staff. This position will lead a team of approx. 5 direct reports and at times additional contractors. Culture: At all times the Manager, Material Procurement shall operate with the highest ethical standards and in full compliance with internal controls, policies, procedures, regulations, and laws. Accountable through supply base partners to execute Entergy’s Local Spend objectives. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS Minimum education and experience required of the position Supply Chain degree or bachelor’s degree in business, Accounting, Engineering, or related discipline and 8+ years of experience in materials/warehousing, purchasing, contracts or project management. Strong knowledge of Supply Chain Management fundamentals. Strong knowledge of interfacing departments' processes and priorities. Uses focused listening to understand others' perspectives. Learn new information and skills quickly. Strong Performance Improvement focus. Demonstrated ability to apply applicable codes and regulations, including UCC, Contract Law and FERC. Working knowledge of all required computer systems including knowledge of Inventory, Materials or Contracts computer systems. Technical understanding of generation principles and operations. This role develops, implements, and maintains knowledgesharing and enablement programs focused on AI, including generative AI, analytics, data platforms, and automation, while ensuring employees across the company can confidently adopt and apply AI capabilities. The Specialist also works directly with business customers to understand their needs, provide guidance on AI tools and techniques, and empower them to successfully adopt AI in their own workflows. Additionally, the Specialist helps drive continuous improvement of all training and enablement programs by evaluating effectiveness, gathering insights, and contributing to the evolution of customer engagement, enablement processes, and AI literacy across the organization. JOB SUMMARY/PURPOSE The ServiceNow Discovery Administrator is responsible for the design, configuration, operation, and continuous improvement of ServiceNow Discovery and related ITOM capabilities within the enterprise ServiceNow platform. This role is expected to effectively use AI to maintain the health and accuracy of the Configuration Management Database (CMDB) by ensuring that Discovery processes reliably identify, classify, and reconcile configuration items (CIs) across on-premises and cloud infrastructure environments. The Discovery Administrator collaborates with infrastructure, security, and IT service management teams to align CMDB data to the Common Service Data Model (CSDM) and to support operational and ITIL governance objectives. This position plays a critical role in ensuring data integrity, enabling service mapping accuracy, and supporting broader ITSM and ITOM process maturity. JOB DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES MID Server Administration Install, configure, and maintain MID Servers across relevant network segments. Monitor MID Server health, availability, and upgrade cycles; coordinate patching and version alignment with platform releases. Troubleshoot MID Server connectivity, authentication, and performance issues. Discovery Configuration & Scheduling Configure and maintain Discovery schedules, behaviors, IP ranges, and scan targets. Configure and validate credential sets for discovery access. Monitor Discovery dashboards/logs; apply AI-assisted log analysis and anomaly detection to proactively identify failures before they compound into CMDB data quality degradation. Coordinate with infrastructure teams on configurations required for Discovery. Develop, maintain, extend, and troubleshoot Discovery patterns as required for successful discovery. CMDB Data Quality & Governance Monitor and improve CMDB health metrics including discovered CI completeness, accuracy, compliance, and relationship integrity before issues affect downstream ITSM processes. Configure and manage IRE rules to minimize duplicate CIs across multiple ingest sources, e.g., integrations, service graph connectors, import sets, etc. Work with CI and process owners to ensure discovery data is available and supports their desired outcomes. Use AI-generated insights to surface and resolve recurring patterns in CI population failures, stale relationship data, and discovery coverage gaps. Align Discovery operations with Change Management, Incident Management, and Asset Management workflows. Support audit and compliance activities requiring accurate, verified CMDB data. Documentation, Reporting & Communication Develop and maintain operational runbooks, configuration documentation, and standard operating procedures for Discovery. Create and maintain dashboards on Discovery coverage, discovered CI health, MID Server status, and open data quality issues. Communicate outages, incidents, or data quality issues clearly to affected teams. Platform Awareness & Continuous Improvement Stay current with ServiceNow release notes, ITOM product updates, and Discovery best practices. Evaluate and recommend improvements to Discovery architecture, coverage, and tooling, including opportunities to apply AI and machine learning to drive continuous efficiency gains. Participate in platform upgrade testing cycles to validate Discovery and CMDB functionality. Mentor junior team members and provide knowledge transfer on Discovery operations. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS Minimum education and experience required of the position: Required Bachelor’s degree in IT, IS, Computer Science, or a related field (or equivalent experience). 3+ years’ hands-on experience with ServiceNow discovery, CMDB, or ITOM. Working knowledge of ITIL service management processes, particularly Configuration Management and Change Management. Preferred ServiceNow CIS-Discovery, CSA, or other relevant certifications a plus. Experience in regulated, complex, or enterprise environments. Familiarity with network concepts, e.g., TCP/IP, DNS, SNMP, and firewall/ACLs. Familiarity with patching tools, scanners, monitoring platforms and AWS environments. jobs.description: Job Title: Environmental Analyst III - Sr Lead Work Place Flexibility: Hybrid Legal Entity: Entergy Services, LLC Please note: Authorization to work in the United States is a precondition to employment in this position. Entergy will not sponsor candidates for work visas for this position. ***This position may be filled as an Analyst III, Sr. or Sr. Lead depending on the candidate's experience and qualifications. *** Job Summary/Purpose Seeking an individual with experience in providing services in support of environmental compliance monitoring and reporting systems. The primary responsibility of this position is to serve as a Continuous Emissions Monitoring Systems (CEMS) Subject Matter Expert (SME) within the Centralized Environmental Services team, supporting emission monitoring activities across Entergy’s fleet of generating units. The incumbent will be responsible for development and implementation of processes and systems required to ensure compliance with environmental laws and regulations under the Clean Air Act (CAA). This position is designated as a Safety Sensitive position and is subject to mandatory pre-employment and random drug testing. Job Duties/Responsibilities Serve as an enterprise-wide CEMS SME for environmental laws and regulations under CAA including, but not limited to, 40 C.F.R. Part 75 (Acid Rain & Emission Monitoring Programs), 40 C.F.R. Part 60 (New Source Performance Standards) and 40 C.F.R. Part 63 (National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants). Comprehensive knowledge of environmental regulations for the research, development, and writing of regulatory Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC) procedures, plans, and test protocols in accordance with federal and state compliance reporting requirements. Review and assemble required initial/recurring performance specification test data (RATA, Linearity, CGA, 7-Day Calibration Error, Opacity Calibration Error Test, PM Testing, etc.) to prepare system certification report submittals for environmental systems. Complete and submit quarterly electronic data reports (EDRs) and monitoring plan updates in the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) Emissions Collection and Monitoring Plan System (ECMPS). Oversee data acquisition handling systems (DAHS). Environmental Systems Corp. (ESC) and StackVision experience preferred. Guide troubleshooting of CEMS hardware (i.e., Analyzers and associated equipment). Work in partnership with Environmental Operational Support team and Environmental Project Services team to assist in ensuring regulatory compliance, identify potential compliance risks and develop risk mitigation plans, as necessary. Provide regulatory analysis of complex rules and regulations pertaining to CEMS which impact Entergy operations across Power Delivery, Power Generation and Nuclear business functions. Draft and distribute concise, timely and accurate written communications, review routine reports and interface with state/federal agencies on Entergy’s behalf to arrive at favorable solutions. Engage with industry groups including, but not limited to, Eddison Electric Institute (EEI), Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI), and ESC User Group. Participate in other environmental duties and special projects as assigned. Manage records and documentation pertaining to compliance programs in accordance with the records retention policy. Identify and execute continuous improvement opportunities. Participate as a team member of the Environmental system outage emergency operations and restoration organization for major storm events. Strong Microsoft tool skills (Word, Excel, and PowerPoint). jobs.title: Lead, Control Ops Coordinator
jobs.description: Job Title: Lead, Control Ops Coordinator Work Place Flexibility: Onsite Legal Entity: Entergy Texas, Inc.-GTX Entergy’s Power Generation group operates a fleet of 28 active natural gas, coal, oil, hydroelectric and solar facilities with the capacity to generate nearly 17,000 megawatts and is building or acquiring more than 3,000 megawatts of new natural gas generation to join its 30,000 megawatts of nuclear, natural gas, coal, oil, hydroelectric and solar facilities. JOB SUMMARY/DESCRIPTION: Responsible for assigning work and providing work direction to employees on same shift. Ensures the safe and reliable operation and maintenance of the plant to meet system needs. Accountable for reporting to Team Leaders any equipment or employee issues as well as overseeing after hours contractor activities as required. JOB DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES: Ensures assigned work within the plant results in safe and reliable operation. Facilitates and coordinates Shift Safety meetings / Job Briefings for all personnel on the same shift. Promotes and ensures a safe work environment, including use of Human Performance tools. Ensures adherence to all safety procedures and policies for all employees working the same shift.Provides work direction in regard to daily operations and maintenance activities for employees assigned to same shift while working a rotating 12 hour shift schedule. Works overtime as required. Works with Team Leaders, Planner Schedulers, and Engineers to develop work packages for shift employees and determine material requirements as necessary.Makes real time decisions and provides work direction in regard to the operation of the equipment in a safe, efficient and reliable manner, at times under critical and stressful situations. Operates boiler, turbine, and generator manually during emergencies. Performs startup and shutdown functions of boiler, turbine, generator and associated equipment as required per instructions from the Energy Management Organization Dispatchers. When un-planned absences occur after hours, ensures adequate shift coverage through contact of other qualified personnel.Provides leadership within the workgroup including mentoring and training others and ensuring their performance of assigned tasks. structured_description.about: Senior-level procurement specialist supporting Entergy's capital projects across power generation and renewable energy portfolios. Partners with Capital Projects, Power Development, and Power Generation leadership to drive commercial strategy, supplier management, and contract optimization for major capital initiatives.
structured_description.responsibilities:
- Develop and maintain stakeholder relationships across Capital Projects, Power Development, and Power Generation organizations to ensure supply chain engagement
- Develop commercial strategies and contract plans aligned to project needs; maximize leverage through aggregation and value optimization across price, terms, performance standards, and service levels
- Lead sourcing of contracts and agreements, including detailed RFx price breakdowns and vendor pricing model analysis
- Manage supplier relationship performance through contract management processes, including claims, disputes, and change order administration
- Execute contract governance and oversee supplier performance management in collaboration with project managers
- Support identification, development, and execution of projects within Entergy's Project Delivery System (stage gate process)
- Ensure alignment of project behaviors to contract requirements and manage compliance to contract provisions
- Collaborate with business units, Category Management, Supplier Diversity, and other stakeholders to deploy capital funds in line with Entergy's strategies
- Actively promote strong safety behaviors and perform storm role duties as assigned
- Establish and maintain professional supplier relationships based on highest ethical business practices and Entergy's Standards of Conduct
structured_description.qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Business, Accounting, Engineering, Legal, or related discipline with minimum 9-12+ years of combined supplier contracting, capital projects, or related supply chain experience; OR minimum 16+ years of supplier contracting, capital projects, or related supply chain experience in lieu of degree
- Minimum 6+ years' supply chain experience in capital projects contracting and procurement
- Skillful application of commercial management processes (plan, strategy, source, and perform)
- Skillful application of market intelligence to assess supply market status and evolution
- Knowledge of Entergy's policies, processes, and their application to contracts
- Skillful in creating capital project contracting strategies and methodologies (e.g., EPC, Fixed Price, T&M)
- Skillful in creating negotiation strategies and leading negotiations for complex contracts
- Knowledge of business and supply chain operations within Entergy, including HEBAP and supply chain systems
- Skillful application of project management principles to ensure systematic completion of assignments
- Financial acumen and ability to apply commercial skills to capital projects
- Understanding of technical aspects of Entergy's business model, capital projects, and key business interfaces
structured_description.desired:
- MBA or other relevant advanced degree
- Certification from an industry accreditation organization such as ISM or ASCM
- Ability to coach other supply chain personnel in capital projects technical tools and techniques
structured_description.location_details: Hybrid, 3 days/week in office, based in Jackson, MS with travel to Vicksburg and Greenville, MS. Applicants from Vicksburg or Greenville considered with travel to Jackson. Out-of-area applicants expected to relocate; relocation assistance not available.

structured_description.about: Senior Security Risk Coordinator for Entergy's Enterprise Security Program, serving as a security and risk subject matter expert. This role coordinates cyber and physical risk management processes across enterprise and operational technology environments, assesses security exceptions, and presents risk insights to executive leadership. You'll manage critical infrastructure protection, logical and physical security controls, and data protection measures while ensuring security posture aligns with target risk thresholds.
structured_description.responsibilities:
- Lead and enhance risk assessment programs for new technologies, critical infrastructure protection, logical cyber and physical security controls, and data protection measures
- Identify, evaluate, and prioritize risk treatment; conduct security reviews of corporate and operational technology infrastructure
- Develop expertise in technology and regulations to ensure security posture and reliability standards align to target risk thresholds
- Provide security risk expertise and guidance to diverse Entergy enterprise and operational technology stakeholders
- Execute and create security risk management program practices; enforce security policies and requirements
- Lead creation, maintenance, and implementation of enterprise, operational, and critical infrastructure protection risk activities
- Apply cybersecurity and risk management framework knowledge to drive risk identification across the enterprise
- Design and communicate risk details during risk ranking sessions; identify risk trends
- Track and manage risks identified through security exception processes or cyber/physical risk review processes
- Develop key risk indicator (KRI) metrics and reporting processes for executive reporting and dashboards using GRC platforms and AI risk methods
- Coordinate with peer Chief Security Officer functions to address security gaps through the risk exception process
- Liaise with Lines of Business on security and reliability risks from exceptions or new technology initiatives
- Guide business unit stakeholders on mitigation strategies for requested exceptions
- Facilitate line of business understanding of mission-critical business process impacts
- Develop and assist in data and risk management process and procedure development
- Assist in data protection and privacy program governance and oversight activities
structured_description.qualifications:
- Bachelor's Degree in Information Systems, Information Assurance, Risk Management, or related field
- 5+ years of information security, critical information protection, information technology, risk management, data analysis, or project management experience
- Planning, organizational, and project management skills with detail and process-oriented mindset
- Problem-solving and decision-making ability
- Written and verbal communication skills with ability to explain complex issues clearly and concisely
- Interpersonal skills including teamwork, facilitation, and negotiation
- Highly collaborative with cross-functional working ability and relationship-building capability
structured_description.desired:
- Understanding of risk management frameworks (NIST 800-39, NISTIR 8286, Open FAIR, COSO Enterprise Risk Management)
- Understanding of logical and physical security technologies and controls (NIST CSF, NIST 800-53)
- Understanding of privacy protection best practices and technical requirements
- Experience with Archer GRC, ServiceNow GRC, or other GRC platforms
- Experience with Microsoft Power BI or other data analytics tools
- Knowledge of quantitative risk analysis and other risk management platforms
- Certified Information Systems Manager (CISM)
- Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
- Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control (CRISC)
- Certified in the Governance of Enterprise IT (CGEIT)
- Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA)
- Certified Protection Professional (CPP)
structured_description.location_details: Hybrid role available in The Woodlands TX, New Orleans LA, Baton Rouge LA, Little Rock AR, or Jackson MS. Up to 25% travel required.

jobs.title: Senior Counsel or Assistant General Counsel (Environmental)
jobs.description: Work Place Flexibility: Onsite Legal Entity: Entergy Services, LLC ***This role will be filled as a Senior Counsel or Assistant General Counsel, depending on the candidate’s qualifications and experience. This role may be filled in Jackson, MS; Little Rock, AR; The Woodlands, TX; New Orleans, LA; or Washington, D.C.*** Job Summary/Purpose Provides first-rate environmental legal advice covering a broad range of environmental media, including air, water, and waste, and environmental subject matter areas. Provides exceptional client service to internal stakeholders by delivering timely, clear, and practical legal guidance tailored to business needs. Serves as a trusted strategic advisor on environmental matters across the Company’s operations, providing practical solutions that balance legal risk with business objectives. Anticipates and evaluates environmental risks across the Company’s operations and commercial transactions, ensuring issues are surfaced early and addressed effectively. Functions effectively within the larger Company, providing direct support to operations leadership and supporting Entergy’s communications, investor relations, external reporting, corporate development, and similar functions concerning environmental issues and litigation. Specific Job Duties/Responsibilities Manage and advise management on legal aspects of the Company's environmental regulatory compliance and responses to any enforcement actions related to the Company's nuclear, fossil, and renewable generating fleet and transmission and distribution operations. Manage and advise on the Company's litigation involving environmental matters. Identify and advise on environmental permitting and other environmental risks in the context of operations, commercial transactions and new projects. Identify potential environmental risks associated with commercial transactions and provide timely, practical advice to support business decision‑making. Supervise and manage outside counsel and consultants engaged to assist with environmental litigation, regulatory, permitting, compliance, and enforcement matters. Advise on environmental legal aspects of the Company's regulatory and other proceedings. Interface with state and federal agency staff on compliance, enforcement, and permitting matters. General Job Duties/Responsibilities Handle routine tasks without supervision and solve difficult problems with minimal supervision. Apply legal principles and knowledge to analyzing business conduct and evaluating compliance with regulatory requirements. Demonstrate in-depth environmental expertise and substantial relevant experience related to the electric utility industry. With only general guidance from supervisors or input from outside counsel, analyze key issues, organize thoughts, advocate and present legal points; draft all documents, negotiate necessary matters, and/or perform other assigned job functions. Effectively supervise paraprofessionals and administrative staff; demonstrate interest in developing management skills. Function as a strong team player and demonstrate ability to lead project teams to successful resolution. Deliver difficult or controversial messages to a wide variety of both supportive and adversarial audiences in a highly-skilled manner. Practice focused listening and respectful interaction with others. Keep key organizational functions (e.g., management, communications, external affairs, investor relations) apprised of significant developments in environmental matters. Occasional travel to locations in Arkansas, Mississippi, and Texas to meet client needs. Minimum Requirements Minimum education required of the position A Juris Doctorate is required. Minimum experience required of the position Senior Counsel: 6+ years in a law firm or in-house experience practicing environmental law Handles complex matters independently with minimal supervision. Assistant General Counsel: 9+ years in a law firm or in-house experience practicing environmental law Serves as a senior legal advisor on highly complex and high‑visibility matters; provides leadership on strategy and cross‑functional initiatives. Preffered: 12+ years of law firm, in-house, or regulatory experience practicing environmental law Preferred/Desired Experience Extensive experience with environmental issues for the power generation industry, including environmental laws and regulations pertaining to all environmental media. Previous experience representing or regulating electric utilities highly preferred. Previous law firm experience highly preferred. Experience practicing environmental law in Mississippi, Arkansas, and/or Texas highly preferred. . Minimum knowledge, skills, and abilities required of the position Highly skilled in complex analysis and in trouble shooting/problem solving issues. Established track record in regulatory, permitting, and compliance matters across multiple environmental media. Demonstrated ability to deliver high‑quality timely client service to diverse internal stakeholders Solid grasp of rules, guidelines and Company policies governing environmental issues. Strong, persuasive written and oral communication skills and collaborative skills Detailed electric utility industry knowledge, including in-depth understanding of the Company’s strategic business values and objectives. Desired Profile - Judgment: demonstrated ability to analyze, synthesize and integrate data to make the best decision; well-developed understanding of the strategic implications of any and all decisions; demonstrate willingness to make tough business and people decisions. Attitude: consistently demonstrates a sense of personal accountability and collaboration; consistently demonstrates positive, team-oriented approach to tasks, projects and other requests for assistance. Demonstrates personal resiliency in stressful times and willingness to commit the time and effort to get the job done. Flexibility: demonstrated ability to respond effectively to multiple and/or conflicting client demands. Respectful Treatment of Others: promotes recognition of sensitivity to the needs of others. Integrity: stands up for what is right, even in the face of adversity; recognizes fundamental importance of acting ethically. Comportment: supportive of others. Learning and Self-Insight: accurately sees own strengths and weaknesses and changes behaviors as needed; demonstrates a passion for ongoing growth and development; and demonstrates creativity. Developmental Mindset: helps coach others to grow both as individuals and as part of an integrated team; is willing to give timely and candid feedback to others. Seeks out job assignments that promote personal and professional development. Possesses sufficient self-awareness to change behaviors that may hinder success. jobs.title: Sr Manager, Construction Management
jobs.description: Work Place Flexibility: Onsite Legal Entity: Entergy Services, LLC JOB SUMMARY/PURPOSE: Sr. Manager, Construction Management to lead a high-performing team of construction professionals in the successful execution of Entergy’s system resilience program. A strong leader who is widely respected and trusted by Entergy's Contract Partners and possess the ability to quickly understand construction culture while mentoring others on effective construction leadership. Strong advocate for the partnering process and continuous improvement. This position will be strategically dedicated to a portfolio of transmission and distribution resiliency projects aimed at delivering projects and holding safety as a top priority. Leverage team expertise to optimize portfolio execution to exceed internal, customer, and regulatory requirements while maintaining a competitive edge with operational efficiency. The candidate will lead a team of direct, matrixed, and contract resources in the safe execution of the program with high quality. Ensure that the projects are staffed with qualified construction management professionals and field personnel for the oversight of construction contractors and their subcontractors. The candidate will collaborate closely with major stakeholders, including contractors and support teams at Entergy. The candidate must actively promote workplace safety, participate in site safety initiatives, and help foster a strong safety culture. JOB DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES Serve as visible leader in the execution of a capital portfolio, ensuring alignment with company goals and strategic objectives. Develop and implement construction management frameworks, tools, and methodologies to improve efficiency and consistency. Lead team in developing comprehensive construction plans including work sequence, outages, and resource requirements. Ensures outages are identified to minimize customer impacts, and Risk reviews are completed for those Tier 1 customers and generators. Lead and mentor a team of construction professionals responsible for capital project execution Lead team to execute projects in accordance with the applicable corporate standards, guidelines, policies and processes. Ensures that team members fulfill their responsibilities as required of their roles. Provide technical, operational, and strategic guidance to direct reports and matrixed employees Mentor and build organizational technical knowledge to achieve corporate and project results Communicate and enforce safety standards across all construction activities, including direct oversight of site practices, contractor performance monitoring, and proactive coaching to ensure adherence to safety protocols and leading indicators. Establish/track leading indicators and proactive requirements to ensure safety is considered in all aspects of design and implementation for contractors, Entergy project team members, and the end user. Provides input into the creation of construction quality standards and practices that are owned by the Power delivery Chief Engineer for projects executed by Entergy Project Delivery business unit. Ensure internal/external compliance with all applicable regulations, quality standards, and safety protocols throughout project execution. Build and maintain strategic relationships with internal/external stakeholders including but limited to, project management, engineering, supply chain, suppliers, and construction partners. Communicate clear expectations for safety, quality, and performance; resolve performance issues proactively Manage vendor relationships and negotiate contracts to ensure the delivery of services and materials within project/program expectations. Work with Supply Chain on procurement, negotiation, and administration of construction and equipment supply agreements Work with stakeholder groups and Supply Chain to ensure standards and safety requirements are integrated into all construction contracts. Interface with all local, state, and federal regulatory agencies regarding specific project needs where appropriate Track construction costs across contractors to drive cost competitiveness; monitor cost performance against budget and identify cost-saving opportunities Monitor contractor performance in safety, schedule, cost, quality of work, and contractual compliance Establish, track, and report KPIs to measure portfolio execution and performance Communicate effectively with stakeholders at all levels regarding project progress, risks, and opportunities Foster a culture of continuous improvement and innovation in construction management processes Participate in lessons-learned reviews and process optimization initiatives Develop construction leaders and create a construction leadership pipeline to ensure organizational capability and succession planning. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:Minimum education: Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or related field OR 4 years equivalent/related work experience (in addition to the Minimum Experience requirement) in lieu of a degree. Preferred: Advanced Degree Preferred - MBA, Masters in Engineering, Construction, Project Management. Minimum experience: 8 years in Utility industry or equivalent relevant experience in capital project management and 3 years supervisory experience. Preferred candidate would have at least 5 years of transmission construction experience plus 2 or more years of power generation plant major project experience. Minimum knowledge, skills and abilities: Engaged leader with a documented legacy of strategic leadership with specific accomplishments in successfully delivering capital projects/portfolios. Demonstrated ability to lead teams to effectively achieve desired results and leading in a matrixed environment. Solid understanding of construction fundamentals and stage-gate processes focused on safely delivering a large portfolio of Power Delivery projects with cost, schedule and scope certainty. Expert in project and construction management fundamentals. Expert in risk and contingency management. Skilled at leading and influencing across organizations, partnering with contract firms, negotiation, obtaining stakeholder input and support, driving continuous improvement ideas, improving organizational health, transforming organizations and improving customer centricity. Able to build, motivate and inspire effective teams and leverage team diversity. Expert at managing conflict, providing clear direction/role clarity and developing employees. Comfortable engaging in crucial conversations. Knowledge of the practical application of engineering science and technology for distribution and transmission systems. This includes applying principles, techniques and procedures to the design, construction, commissioning and operations of Transmission Substation, Transmission Lines, Distribution Lines, or Electrical Power Generating facilities. Knowledge of materials, methods, and the tools involved in the construction or repair of Transmission Substation, Transmission Lines, Distribution Lines, or Electrical Power Generating facilities. History of safe performance, active safety involvement and participation and strong desire for a safer workplace. Possess excellent written and verbal communication skills. Demonstrated cross-functional project leadership experience, team performance skills, service mindset approach, and the ability to act as a trusted advisor. Knowledge of Effective Estimating Practices. Strong leadership, negotiation, analytical, interpersonal & group communication skills. Strong Planning\Organization\Time Management skills. Any certificates, licenses, etc.: Preferred: PMP (Project Management Professional certification) Preferred: Advanced Degree Other Attributes: Functional Knowledge: Requires in-depth understanding of concepts, theories and principles in own discipline and basic knowledge of other disciplines. Business Expertise: Applies understanding of the industry and how own area

jobs.description: Job Title: Process Owner Work Place Flexibility: Onsite Legal Entity: Entergy Mississippi, LLC **This posting will fill 2 vacancies** At Entergy, we’ve been planning for the future for more than 100 years. We’ve experienced a lot of change, generating power first from sawdust to splitting atoms, harnessing sunlight, and using abundant, clean and efficient natural gas. We are leading the clean energy transformation for the utility industry and continue to explore alternative technologies. We are on the verge of a monumental technology convergence, where reality swiftly catches up to possibility. The utility of the future does much more than keep the lights on and the gas flowing. It’s knowledgeable and skillful workforce will solve challenges and fuel a brighter, smarter, cleaner, and more prosperous future for everyone. Having the lowest retail electricity rates of any utility in the United States drives economic growth within Entergy’s region, a key ingredient to sustained growth for any utility. We also believe in an inclusive workforce committed to personal and professional growth is critical to our success. We place a high priority on developing talent to meet current and future needs, giving employees opportunities to grow their careers their way. We’ve committed over the next three decades to reduce our carbon emissions from our operations to net-zero by 2050. Entergy’s Power Generation group operates a fleet of more than 30 owned, leased, or operated natural gas, coal, hydro and solar plants, with a total engineering capacity exceeding 20,000 megawatts. Entergy continues to build or acquire megawatts from new hydrogen capable natural gas units, solar, wind and other technologies to complement its existing megawatts of nuclear, natural gas, coal, hydroelectric, and solar facilities. Entergy is also on the leading edge of pursuing carbon capture technology on new and existing combined cycle plants to reach carbon neutral goals. jobs.description: Job Title: Manager Service Delivery, IT (Customer Systems and Innovation) Work Place Flexibility: Hybrid Legal Entity: Entergy Services, LLC ***The preferred location for this position is The Woodlands, TX. JOB SUMMARY/PURPOSE The Manager of Customer Systems will serve as a key member of the Customer Systems and innovation leadership team with responsibility for the development, implementation and maintenance of application services for the Customer Organization. The Mgr. will devise strategies to improve business practices, choose appropriate applications and program new digital solutions with focus across customer contact, sales, and service value chains. The Mgr. is responsible for understanding the business, aligning IT strategy with overall business strategy and Entergy strategic imperatives, assisting in project prioritization, ensuring that projects align with the IT standards, and that all respective customer systems are reliable and secure. The Mgr. will lead teams responsible for the applications supporting the Customer functions. The application portfolio will include but not be limited to digital customer self-service channels, customer relationship management, automated customer messaging, and internal customer service solutions. The role is responsible for delivering assigned projects on time, on budget, with first time quality, and adherence to business requirements while standardizing/rationalizing technical platforms, as well as operational oversight of the day-to-day support activities performed. JOB DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES For the assigned portfolio of application technologies: Be able to drive improvements that impact our commercial customers journey through leading teams to develop improvements in Salesforce and AWS. Establish and maintain business relationships with customers to ensure value is delivered to internal and external customers. Develop strategic plans and roadmaps for new applications to support business objectives and increase the sharing of information across customer systems (Service Cloud, AWS, Datacloud, AgentForce, View Outage Map). Manage a team of development and support personnel that focuses to deliver value by working on break/fix, requests, defects, and ideas. Support major events as part of the Incident Management process to ensure systems are meeting expectations and resolve all system issues as they may arrive. Entergy owns and operates power plants with approximately 26,000 megawatts of electric generating capacity, including 6,000 megawatts of nuclear power. Entergy delivers electricity to 3 million utility customers in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Texas. Tracing its history to 1913 and headquartered in New Orleans, Louisiana, Entergy has annual revenues of $11 billion and more than 12,000 employees. The company’s utility business provides electric retail and wholesale power to customers in four states through five utility operating companies: Entergy Arkansas, LLC; Entergy Louisiana, LLC; Entergy Mississippi, LLC; Entergy New Orleans, LLC; and Entergy Texas, Inc. Entergy also delivers natural gas services to 200,000 customers in New Orleans and parts of Baton Rouge, Louisiana. Entergy is winding down its wholesale generation business, which provides power to wholesale customers primarily from our one remaining nuclear facility located in the northern United States. The electric utility industry is rapidly changing, and Entergy is entering an exciting period of growth as we prepare for the future. We are building the premier utility, a utility that delivers sustainable value to all its stakeholders – our customers, employees, communities, and owners – as measured by strong net promoter scores, high levels of service, superior and affordable products and services, highly skilled and engaged employees, and industry-leading financial performance. We are focusing our sights on three key priorities – customer centricity, continuous improvement, and creating a culture of belonging for our employees. Join us as we take the next step on our journey to building the premier utility. structured_description.about: Nuclear Reactor Operator role at Constellation Energy, the nation's largest producer of clean energy. You will operate nuclear power stations safely and efficiently in accordance with NRC-licensed procedures and technical specifications. This position includes an Initial License Training (ILT) program leading to NRC Reactor Operator licensure, with classroom instruction, study, exams, and field training provided by the company.
structured_description.responsibilities:
- Operate the nuclear power plant in accordance with approved procedures and Technical Specifications Limiting Conditions for Operation
- Monitor reactor and assigned control room panels to ensure operation remains within established parameters
- Notify the Unit Supervisor of unusual or unexpected conditions
- Maintain awareness of activities and work impacting the unit; assist other Reactor Operators as needed
- Maintain shift narrative logs documenting all significant unit activities
- Perform clearance activities and electrical switching from the Control Room
- Coordinate liquid radwaste releases and transfers with Reactor Operators and Radwaste Equipment Operators
- Complete NRC Reactor Operator licensing requirements including classroom lessons, study, exams, and field training
- Pass company and NRC-administered licensing exams
- Serve on the Emergency Response Organization and participate in fire brigade qualifications
- Support on-call rotating shift coverage including holidays and weekends
structured_description.qualifications:

- Pass the Plant Operator Selection System (POSS) and Basic Math and Science Test (BMST) pre-employment assessments
- Pass NRC-required physical examination for licensed operators, including ability to wear a respirator and 20-pound oxygen tank
- Obtain unescorted access authorization at Constellation nuclear facilities
- Meet one of the following experience pathways: (1) 6 months as a qualified non-licensed operator at Constellation (all power block and safety system duties) plus 18 months total power plant experience; (2) 12 months as qualified non-licensed operator at comparable nuclear facility or 18 months at non-comparable nuclear facility plus 18 months total power plant experience; (3) 6 months as an active NRC-licensed RO at comparable facility or 12 months at non-comparable commercial power reactor plus 18 months total power plant experience; (4) 18 months in Navy Reactor program (Reactor Operator, Engineering Officer of the Watch, or equivalent); or (5) 27 months in preoperational, startup, operational, design, construction, technical support, maintenance, or training roles at petrochemical, process, or steam propulsion plants
structured_description.location_details: On-site at Constellation nuclear power station; on-call rotating shifts including holidays and weekends; must be able to wear respirator and 20-pound oxygen tank for fire brigade duties.

Constellation is seeking Initial License Trainees (ILT) to become a licensed Senior Reactor Operator (SRO) supporting Braidwood Nuclear Power Sation in Braceville, IL. Must have 1.5 years after qualification. Degree from a 4-year program or equivalent in engineering, engineering technology, or physical sciences, or professional engineer license, and more than 1.5 years as a qualified non-licensed operator or Staff member, Supervisor or Manager in work control, operations, engineering, outage management, maintenance, radiation protection, chemistry, or accredited training at a comparable (BWR or PWR) facility. Constellation is seeking Initial License Trainees (ILT) to become a licensed Senior Reactor Operator (SRO) supporting Bryon Nuclear Power Station located in Byron, IL. Must have 1.5 years after qualification. Degree from a 4-year program or equivalent in engineering, engineering technology, or physical sciences, or professional engineer license, and more than 1.5 years as a qualified non-licensed operator or Staff member, Supervisor or Manager in work control, operations, engineering, outage management, maintenance, radiation protection, chemistry, or accredited training at a comparable (BWR or PWR) facility. Current or previous SRO Instructor certification and 4 years experience at a comparable facility or 6 years experience at a non-comparable facility. Maintain minimum access requirement or unescorted access requirements, as applicable, and favorable medical examination and/or testing in accordance with position duties.

Primary Purpose of Position The Engineering Business Analyst serves as the centralized coordination and integration point for Engineering planning, governance, and business execution at the site. Coordinate the site Asset Management Plan and key indicators associated with the department budget. This includes prep for the spring and fall Senior Vice President AMP calls, validating the AMP against the site Top 15/30 modification lists, facilitate department contracts, schedule and hold department accountable to the business planning overall timeline. Constellation is seeking Initial License Trainees (ILT) to become a licensed Senior Reactor Operator (SRO) supporting Calvert Cliffs Generating Station located in Lusby, MD. Utilizes the Safety Report process, Continuous Improvement process, and other procedures to ensure a healthy safety culture exists within the Transportation Department. Maintain accurate and comprehensive records in the CRM for all business development activities. Identifies opportunities for process improvements, cost reductions, and increased efficiency within flight operations. Implements new technologies, training programs, or best practices to enhance productivity and safety. Accepts and performs additional duties as assigned by the Chief Pilot. Primary Purpose of Position The Senior Analyst, Credit Risk is responsible for a credit portfolio within the designated regions. As a member of the credit organization, this position will require an advanced understanding of the physical and financial products offered by the Company and the marketplace in order to properly assess and monitor counterparty credit/risk issues. The incumbent is closely aligned with the business and functional leaders throughout the organization and is expected to foster and maintain strong working partnerships with their respective peers. Also coordinates effectively with Receivables team to monitor aged receivables to ensure timely collection. Assist on presentations to Senior Management that include credit decisions and recommendations, while highlighting top credit risks within the organization. As directed by Credit leadership, lead the coordination, maintenance, and implementation of improved reporting and functionality of Credit Risk systems. Primary Purpose of Position The successful candidate will be an integral part of the risk management function of Constellation. Use quantitative methods to develop new frameworks and perform ad-hoc analyses for risk limits and guidelines as required by business activity, market events, or changes in risk appetite Raise potential issues to Market Risk Management Enforces compliance with trading limits as well as market risk policies and procedures. Calculates, streamlines, and automates risk metric processes to improve efficiency and maintain high quality standards. Establishes and strengthens active dialogue with portfolio managers to understand and quantify emerging market risks and hedge strategies. Prepare analysis for Risk Management Committee meetings and provides special or ad hoc analysis to support various management meetings. Primary Purpose of Position Responsible for providing technical, regulatory, and programmatic direction for the environmental functional area of Constellation Projects & Services team. Primary Purpose of Position Responsible for supporting Constellation's Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) and the Department of Transportation (DOT) Fitness for Duty (FFD) programs. This position will aid in ensuring that Constellation personnel are fit for duty by avoiding substance abuse and not being under the influence of any substance, whether legal or illegal, that could impair their ability to perform their duties safely and competently. The Fitness for Duty Programs apply to employees and contract workers who work at Constellation, Constellation parents, and/or subsidiaries. These programs comply with the requirements of NRC Part 26, (employees and contract workers who work at Constellation's Nuclear Clean Energy Center's and/or hold positions that require them to be a part of the fitness for duty program, I.e., Emergency Response Organization (ERO Members) and Fitness for Duty Administrator (FFDA), DOT Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration, 49 CFR Part 382, and for Constellation's pipeline facilities, the DOT Pipeline, and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration requirements, 49 CFR Part 199. This position is a part of a multi-disciplinary team and must work closely with contractors, vendors, and other professionals outside of Corporate Access Authorization and Fitness for Duty (AA/FFD). Primary Duties and Accountabilities This individual will play a critical role in ensuring a safe and drug-free work environment for all employees and contractors and ensure compliance with Company policies and procedures, as well as regulatory guidelines. This includes, maintaining accurate records of test results and employee information and enter all testing into the Fitness for Duty database. Conduct fitness for duty testing at various work locations to maintain compliance with NRC and DOT regulations, as well as company policy. They will provide guidance and direction to employees and their supervisors regarding the drug and alcohol testing process. Testing includes, but is not limited to pre-access, random, follow-up, post-accident, and for cause. Assist in the implementation of Constellation's Nuclear Fitness for Duty Program to ensure compliance with the Code of Federal Regulation(s). Maintain extensive knowledge of Code of Federal Regulations (10 CFR 73.55, 10 CFR 73.56, 10 CFR 73.57, 10 CFR 26, Regulatory Guide 5.66), Nuclear Energy Institute (NEI) document(s) 03-01-Regulated), NRC Inspection Procedures, and Site Security Plan. Generate and implement Fitness for Duty processes with the highest level of confidentiality. On call 24/7 for Access Authorization & Fitness for Duty concerns/incidents; ability to respond outside of normal business hours. Maintain knowledge and understanding of Security Operations procedures, polices, and processes Directly work with corporate AA/FFD management in the coordination of employee in-processing for UA/UAA and Fitness for Duty concerns Support site In-processing and outage schedule by working with outage management to implement cost effective timely in-processing. Travel is required Conduct Blind Performance testing as described in 10CFR26. Qualify and maintain training and certifications for breath alcohol and urine specimen collector. Assist with testing records and enter all results into the Fitness for Duty database. Support Fitness for Duty program for other areas of the business to include: Constellation Generation (Nuclear FFD), Department of Transportation FFD Program, Power FFD Program, etc. Qualify and execute the functions as a Level 1 and 2 Reviewing Official in support of in processing activities. Qualify and maintain qualifications responsible for the operation of Personnel Access Data System (PADS); ensure compliance with NEI/PADS policies, procedures, and system security requirements. Perform other job assignments and duties as directed by management or pursuant to company policy, including but not limited to emergency response, departmental coverage, call outs, and support of outage activities in positions outside the department. Minimum Qualifications High school diploma/GED or equivalent with 2 years of related experience Maintain minimum access requirements or unescorted access requirements, as applicable, and favorable medical examination and/or testing in accordance with position duties Preferred Qualifications RO1/RO2 qual 2 or more years Nuclear Security FFD experience Training and certifications for breath alcohol and urine specimen collector. Demonstrated knowledge and proficiency in the NRC Part 26 FFD drug and alcohol collection process. Previous Fitness for Duty or related experience. Knowledge and proficiency in NRC and/or DOT drug and alcohol collection regulations. Experience working with vendors/contractors.

Primary Purpose of Position The Cycle Manager manages the Cycle Plan for the Nuclear Clean Energy Centers (CECs) and is responsible for sequencing of work within the plan, taking into consideration the CEC design configuration Technical Specifications, Maintenance Rule, Probabilistic Safety Analysis, personnel and CEC safety, material condition, resource management, regulatory compliance, to safely optimize electrical production and minimize maintenance costs. Responsible for maintaining performance towards the various CEC backlog and Material Condition Improvement Plan (MCIP) related goals. Establishes the scope and boundaries of the cycle plan and monitors the performance of the Cycle Schedulers. Chairs or participates in the Station Oversight Committee (SOC). Performs screening of new issue reports. Drives the management of CEC backlogs, maintaining a balance between preventative, corrective, and elective maintenance work completion for effective continuous material condition improvement. Perform other job assignments and duties as directed by management or pursuant to company policy, including but not limited to emergency response, departmental coverage, call outs, and support of outage activities in positions outside the department. Constellation (Formerly known as Exelon Nuclear) is the nation’s largest producer of carbon-free energy and sustainable solutions to millions of homes, institutional customers, the public sector, community aggregations and businesses, including three fourths of Fortune 100 companies. Our generation fleet of nuclear, hydro, wind, and solar generation facilities powers more than 20 million homes and businesses, providing 10 percent of all clean power on the grid in the U.S. All told, our fleet is helping to accelerate the nation’s transition to clean energy with more than 32,400 megawatts of capacity and annual output that is nearly 90 percent carbon-free. We provide reliable access to clean power whenever our customers need it, 24 hours per day and 7 days per week. It's important work powered by people with a common set of values. Location- Fitzpatrick Nuclear Station Oswego, NY The SNO is the senior represented Nuclear Operator on a shift. The SNO directs and coordinates the work of all Operators of a lower grade on shift that are engaged in the operation of a Nuclear Power Plant, including the Nuclear Steam Supply System, Turbine Generator and all Auxiliary Equipment and associated 345KV and 115KV Switchyards during plant startup, shutdown, refueling, emergency and normal operating conditions. From an operating standpoint, the SNO is responsible for proper operation of all the Nuclear Power Plant’s equipment within the confines of Technical Specifications, Operating Procedures, Special Procedures and all other procedures that apply to operation of the Nuclear Power Plant. As the Senior Nuclear Operator on the shift, he/she may be present at any point within the Nuclear Power Plant or its associated 345KV or 115KV Switch Yards as conditions dictate so as to most efficiently discharge the duties of the SNO. The SNO may, when conditions or circumstances dictate, assume the duties and responsibilities of the Nuclear Control Operator. (Some of these are core alterations, fuel movement, license requirements and plant emergencies). Special duties include, but are not limited to: Directs (and may perform when conditions and circumstances dictate) the work and duties of lower grade Nuclear Operators. From an operating standpoint, coordinates the activities of personnel working in the plant facilities. Maintains an active interest in the Operations of the Nuclear Power Plant and through reading and study should keep current with the technological advances as they apply to the position of Senior Nuclear Operator. Must have the ability to qualify as a Radiation Protection Self Monitor. Must be the holder of an NRC Reactor Operators License. Must have the ability to direct the work of other employees. Must have the ability to assist in the training of other employees. Must have two years operating experience in a thermal power plant of which a minimum of one year shall be as a NCO or equivalent.

PRIMARY PURPOSE OF POSITION The Sr. Insider Threat Analyst is a member of the Insider Threat Team with primary responsibility for mitigating, identifying, and responding to insider threat security events. Conduct open-source research about industry trends and developments in protecting company assets and countering Insider Threats. Prepare timely written reports which summarize significant industry insider events to draw lessons which can be incorporated into the Insider Threat Program Assist in the development of policy, processes, procedures an associated metrics Produce and deliver insider threat awareness briefings, debriefings, and training activities. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or related 4-year technical degree with 5 + years of experience in IT or cybersecurity, or equivalent combination of education and work experience. Skill in collecting data from a variety of cyber defense resources and ability to interpret information collected to recognize threats. Knowledge of DLP, UEBA, and logging applications; and skill tuning policies within these tools. Knowledge of incident response and handling methodologies. Knowledge of computer networking concepts and protocols, and network security methodologies. Knowledge of host/network access control mechanisms. Knowledge of operating systems. Knowledge of scripting languages. Knowledge of cyber-attack stages and techniques used by malicious insiders. Knowledge of security controls frameworks and ability to assess organizational security posture against these frameworks. Skill in conducting trend analysis PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 5+ years of direct insider threat analysis experience. CISSP, SANS GIAC, or other relevant certifications. Demonstrated skill in modifying and developing UEBA rules through advanced editors and scripting languages. Knowledge of Insider Threat investigations, reporting, investigative tools and laws/regulations. Knowledge of NIST SP 800-53 Cybersecurity Framework. CERT Insider Threat Program Manager Professional Certificate and/or knowledge of Carnegie Mellon's Insider Threat Best Practices. Knowledge of Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management, Communication Compliance and Data Loss Prevention Strong verbal and written communication skills. Ability to effectively convey complex technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences including investigators, senior management, team members and others

Initiates Emergency Plan in accordance with implementing procedure. Implements tagging and system out-of-service requests, including directing others to realign valves, rack out breakers and hang tags. During refueling of the reactor, manipulates controls, drives, etc. and observes nuclear and radiation monitoring instruments in accordance with procedural controls. jobs.description: Engineer – Plant Hatch Summary of Job Duties: We have openings for engineers that may be filled as a system engineer, a program engineer, a component engineer or a design engineer at Plant Hatch in Baxley, GA. Program and component engineers direct implementation of assigned programs and work processes. Engineers at Southern Nuclear may have opportunities to manage special projects. Also, engineers typically take key refueling outage assignments. Future developmental assignments in operations, maintenance, training, or quality assurance often prepare engineers for supervisory and management positions. Engineering assignments typically include on-call duty engineer and emergency plan response requirements.
